articles.title: Malik Nabers' Injury Status for Giants vs. Cowboys Revealed After NFL Rumors Ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: New York Giants fans will not have to wait for Malik Nabers' season debut.
articles.body:
New York Giants fans will not have to wait for Malik Nabers' season debut.

The star wide receiver is officially active for Sunday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys.

The news comes after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported ahead of Sunday night's game that Nabers' "status is best described as murky at best. Very much up in the air for the New York Giants. It does not seem to me like something they are counting on."

The Giants also seemed to be preparing for Nabers' potential absence when they elevated wide receivers Dalen Cambre and Braxton Berrios from the practice squad.

Rapoport described the moves as "insurance."

While Nabers did practice in full leading up to the game against the division-rival Cowboys, he is also coming off a torn ACL that limited him to just four games last season.

Earlier in training camp, the wide receiver took a long-term view on his recovery when asked whether he would be available for Week 1:

"The most important thing is my health," Nabers said. "The most important thing is just completing every milestone that they have in front of me, giving good effort, continuing to come out here and be a great teammate to my teammates."

Nabers is just 23 years old and surely expected to be a franchise cornerstone for years to come in New York.

The LSU product wasted no time establishing himself as a star with 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, and getting him back to that level for the foreseeable future will help the Giants once again become contenders in the NFC East after finishing with a losing record in eight of the last nine seasons.

With Nabers officially active, the Giants should see a huge boost on offense against the Cowboys as they look to start the season with a win.

articles.title: Rex Ryan Says He'd Cut Deshaun Watson After Video Ripping Browns Fans amid Shedeur Sanders QB Battle
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson made headlines last month when he ripped Cleveland Browns fans for booing him during a preseason game, and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan revealed Sunday that would have led to a drastic response if he was in charge of the AFC North team.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson made headlines last month when he ripped Cleveland Browns fans for booing him during a preseason game, and former NFL head coach Rex Ryan revealed Sunday that would have led to a drastic response if he was in charge of the AFC North team.

"No way would I have started him," Ryan said on ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown when discussing Cleveland's decision to start Watson over Shedeur Sanders.

"No way. In fact, I would have cut him. I mean, that press conference. … There's no more important thing than that fan base. No way in hell. I couldn't believe what I was hearing. … I don't care who was the backup, no way would I have kept this guy."

While Watson's comments may have been upsetting to Browns fans and Ryan, cutting him would have been a financial blow for the franchise.

As Mike Ginnitti of Spotrac detailed last month, cutting the quarterback ahead of the 2026 campaign would have left approximately $41 million in a dead cap hit for 2026 and a stunning $86.2 million dead cap hit for 2027.

That is financially unfeasible, regardless of how the organization feels about Watson at this point.

His comments surely didn't help his standing, though, as he did not hold back when discussing Cleveland fans.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said at the time. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think that's a disrespectful thing.

"... Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt.

"What does that have to do with it? What does that have to do anything with my performance? When a person gets hurt, especially from their own city, and they cheer... I had different thoughts on what it was going to be, but it is what it is."

It should be noted he later apologized in his next media availability.

While the Browns couldn't realistically cut Watson as a tenure that has been defined by injuries, suspension and poor play continued, they could have started Sanders instead.

Yet head coach Todd Monken gave the starting nod to the veteran, who will lead the offense in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Cleveland surely hopes Watson returns to the form he demonstrated with the Houston Texans when he was a Pro Bowler for three straight years from 2018 through 2020. Still, it wouldn't be surprising if there is a short leash when it comes to making a quarterback change if he once again struggles to start the 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Russell Wilson Thinks Joe Burrow 'Wants to Leave' Bengals, Predicts Exit if Team Struggles
articles.summary: Former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson debuted as an NFL analyst for CBS on Sunday, and he's already making some bold predictions.
articles.body:
Former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson debuted as an NFL analyst for CBS on Sunday, and he's already making some bold predictions.

During Sunday's episode of NFL Today , Wilson declared, "I'm telling you right now, if it doesn't go well in Cincinnati this year, Joe Burrow is gone. I think he wants to leave."

For his part, Burrow has maintained his commitment to the Bengals. He recently said in an interview with the team's website that he hopes to remain in Cincinnati long-term despite the lack of success in the past few years.

"I'm here for the long haul," Burrow said, per ESPN's Ben Baby . "I'm not going anywhere. I'm just trying to bring a now-or-never mentality to the day-by-day process. If you're not, what are you doing? Attack the day with a championship mindset. The rest will take care of itself."

The Bengals have missed the playoffs in each of the last three years. While Burrow is part of one of the best passing attacks in the league with wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Cincinnati's defense has performed well below expectations. The team signed defensive end Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook in free agency and traded for Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II this offseason.

Burrow also previously declared that he's looking to lead the Bengals to a Super Bowl title this season. While it would be disappointing to fall short of his goals, it would be a massive surprise if he fulfills Wilson's prediction and pushes to leave Cincinnati after this season.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns vs Jacksonville Jaguars NFL Week 1 Live Updates, Highlights and Analysis
articles.summary: It has been a tumultuous offseason in Cleveland. The departure of Myles Garrett. A quarterback controversy. There was drama galore.
articles.body:
It has been a tumultuous offseason in Cleveland. The departure of Myles Garrett. A quarterback controversy. There was drama galore.

Now, however, the time for drama off the field is over. It's time for the Browns to start telling the story of 2026 on the field—Sunday the team will take the field at EverBank Stadium to face a Jacksonville Jaguars team that went 13-4 and won the AFC South in 2025.

It's a game where the Browns are significant underdogs—and a contest that could set the tone for the early portion of the 2026 campaign.

We're going to do some tone-setting of own here at Bleacher Report, tracking all the highlights and happenings from Sunday's showdown. Or beatdown. Whatever.

Trying to maintain some optimism—at least until kickoff.

Almost feel bad for the guy. Waits years to get his shot at being an NFL head coach--and barely gets an NFL team.

Some thoughts regarding yet another Week 1 loss by the Browns--their seventh in the last eight years.

With the exception of that long touchdown throw in garbage time, Watson was worse than his stats--16-of-22 for 205 yards with that score and a pick. But there won't be a change coming under center next week in Tampa.

The run game was non-existent. Watson was the team's leading rusher, and Quinshon Judkins averaged less than three yards per carry.

Perhaps the most disappointing aspect of the performance was the defense. Jacksonville could easily have eclipsed the 360 yards of offense the team had, and the Jaguars converted half of their third downs.

If that's what Cleveland fans have to look "forward" to on a weekly basis, those fans will be actively rooting for the Browns to tank by Thanksgiving.

Granted, it's in a blowout loss, but this 46-yard touchdown throw from Watson to Denzel Boston is both the best throw we've seen from Watson in a dawg's age (see what I did there?) and a nice catch from the second-round rookie.

To be fair, no one expected Jared Verse to be a one-for-one replacement for Myles Garrett in Cleveland.

But Verse did his best Garrett imitation Sunday--or at least his best impression of Garrett's vanishing act last Thursday night.

Verse played the run fairly well, logging four tackles (three solo) and a tackle for loss. But he was a complete non-factor rushing the passer--no sacks, QB hits or even pressures.

The Browns may just be trolling us at this point.

Cleveland finally got some offense going on a drive that included Deshaun Watson's best throw of the afternoon.

The team made it into the red zone and everything.

But back-to-back sacks resulted in a turnover on downs.

Nick Mullens is in for Trevor Lawrence under center for the Jaguars

That Cleveland's offense is hot garbage is not exactly breaking news. That tends to happen when a team has no quarterback. But even without Myles Garrett, the Browns were supposed to at least be decent defensively.

They don't look it. The Browns have allowed over 350 yards in less than three quarters. The Jaguars are piling up 4.7 yards per carry and 7.2 yards per play.

The only reason it isn't 38-3 is that Jacksonville killed their own drive with penalties. The Jags are the only team stopping the Jags in this mess.

The good news is that after a long kickoff return, the Browns finally got inside Jacksonville's five-yard line.

The bad news is that a delay of game penalty cost Cleveland five critical yards, and after a Watson wormburner on third down the team was forced to settle for a short field goal.

Now all the Browns need are four unanswered touchdowns and they'll be right back in this thing!

What else can you really say? Trevor Lawrence is having his way with the Cleveland defense. A scramble-drill turns into a 32-yard scoring strike to Jakobi Meyers.

It was Lawrence's fourth touchdown pass of the game.

Might as well put this out there, because you can bet the rent that fans will be calling for a switch at quarterback in Cleveland.

This Browns fan isn't going to argue that Deshaun Watson is trash. His arm strength is shot. His decision-making is--I legitimately wonder after making $230 million to mostly sit on his butt if he even really cares anymore.

But putting Shedeur Sanders out there is going to fix exactly nothing.

Sanders has no pocket presence. He can't read defenses. Hi decision-making isn't any better than Watson's.

It's like arguing the merits of the electric chair vs. the gas chamber.

Plus, the guy who signs the checks wants Watson--possibly so he can justify giving him that fully guaranteed abomination of a contract.

And in Cleveland, Jimmy Haslam gets what Jimmy Haslam wants.

The Browns commit approximately all the penalties ever on their final drive of the half, and it's 24-bupkus at the break.

Passing: Deshaun Watson (8-for-13, 75 yards, INT)

Rushing: Quinshon Judkins (five carries, 14 yards)

Receiving: Jerry Jeudy (two catches, 26 yards)

Cleveland was outgained 234-95, turned it over twice and barely had 11 minutes of possession.

What was it John McKay said about his team's execution?

Defensive tackle Mason Graham has caught a lot of flak from fans for not making a bigger statistical dent--largely because he was part of the Travis Hunter trade a year ago.

But late in the second quarter, Graham recorded the first full sack of his young career, forcing a Jaguars punt.

The way this game is going, you have to take good news anywhere you can get it.

Well, the Browns managed to avoid turning it over. Even crossed midfield. But outside the first drive of the game (which ended in an INT) the Cleveland offense has been offensive.

Rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion gets the ball punched out by Jaguars linebacker Ventrell Miller. Jags recover, and five plays later Lawrence finds tight end Brenton Strange from 14 yards out.

Another long drive by the Jaguars (11 plays) concludes with a 47-yard field goal from Cam Little, and Jacksonville is up 17-scratch.

The Browns are being embarrassed in just about every way a team can be. Being blown off both lines of scrimmage. Can't cover. Can't tackle. The offense is laughably bad.

Thought it would take until at least Week 3 for the team to hit rock-bottom.

Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker combine for a strip-sack of Watson and it's punting time again as the first quarter ends.

Over the first 15 minutes, the Browns were outgained 138-28.

Nine plays, 74 yards and Trevor Lawrence's second touchdown pass of the quarter and the Browns are down two scores.

Lawrence is eight of 10 for 114 yards and two touchdowns. Parker Washington has four catches for 69 yards and a score.

And someone apparently forgot to tell the Browns defense that the game started.

Well this is going just swimmingly so far--third-down back Dylan Sampson is in the locker room after suffering a knee injury.

Two Quinshon Judkins carries for four yards. One off-target throw to Harold Fannin. And it's Corey Bojorquez time.

Well, it didn't take the Jaguars long to make the Browns pay for the turnover.

Jacksonville drove 59 yards in eight plays over about four minutes before Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington from 30 yards out.

The Browns had a promising early drive going. The team had moved the ball inside Jacksonville's 30-yard line.

And then Deshaun Watson threw a terrible interception--he just didn't see Jags linebacker Foyesade Oluokun.

The season is off to a very Cleveland start.

For what it's worth, this isn't the first time Deshaun Watson has started for the Browns on the road against the Jags.

Watson's stats weren't great back in Week 2 of the 2024 season--186 yards on 22 of 34 pass attempts. But Watson ran for a score, Cleveland's defense balled out, and the Browns won 18-13.

No team in the NFL allowed fewer rushing yards per game than the 85.6 the Jaguars gave up.

Quinshon Judkins will have to earn every yard Sunday, and this is a game Deshaun Watson may have to win with his arm.

Nothing says football and Fall quite like playing a game inside a sauna.

articles.title: Josh Allen Addresses Windy Weather Concerns at Bills' New Stadium in Video with Chris Berman
articles.summary: The new Highmark Stadium still exposes the Buffalo Bills to the elements, but star quarterback Josh Allen is confident the venue can mitigate some of the effects of the historically tough winters in the region.
articles.body:
The new Highmark Stadium still exposes the Buffalo Bills to the elements, but star quarterback Josh Allen is confident the venue can mitigate some of the effects of the historically tough winters in the region.

In an interview with Allen for Sunday NFL Countdown , ESPN's Chris Berman asked the 2024 NFL MVP if he believes the Bills have "solved the wind" with how they built the stadium.

"I think they've solved most of it," Allen said (3:10 mark). "I think it'll still be a little wind in here, but I think it's gonna cut it in half."

The Bills could've eliminated this problem altogether by enclosing Highmark Stadium. That was never part of the plan , though, and Allen told Berman he thought more home fans want outdoor games over sitting in a comfortable dome setting.

Instead, the designers attempted to create "wind confusion," which would theoretically cause less gusts to get down to the field.

The Athletic's Tim Graham said the early reviews weren't totally encouraging after the Bills opened new Highmark during the preseason.

"I've also heard concerns about wind in the concourses, which construction workers have been whispering about for the past year," he reported in August. "They say the wind howls through there. Much was made about the new Highmark Stadium being weatherproof, but the wind and rain already seem like issues. Maybe they won't be on the field, which is what some of the technology was meant to address, but the fans endured Saturday night."

The architects might have to go back to the drawing board.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Gives Surprising Quote on Injury Return After Knee Surgery Before Chiefs vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes knew long ago that he'd return from knee surgery in time for Monday night's season opener against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes knew long ago that he'd return from knee surgery in time for Monday night's season opener against the Denver Broncos.

Jay Glazer reported on Sunday's episode of FOX NFL Pregame that Mahomes told him that he felt capable of playing in Week 1 since the start of the summer.

"He told me two weeks ago, he's like, 'Glaze, I was ready in the first week of June. I can do everything,'" Glazer said.

Mahomes announced last week that he will be able to play in Monday night's matchup without limitations, just nine months removed from knee surgery after tearing his ACL and LCL last season. Glazer noted that Mahomes chose not to wait for his knee swelling to go down before undergoing surgery, which helped accelerate his recovery timeline.

The Chiefs are hoping to return to title contention after missing the playoffs last season, and having Mahomes healthy to start the year is a positive sign.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Benching for Shedeur Sanders Called for by NFL Fans as Browns Trolled in 1st Half
articles.summary: It didn't take two full quarters for Cleveland Browns fans to turn on starting quarterback Deshaun Watson.
articles.body:
It didn't take two full quarters for Cleveland Browns fans to turn on starting quarterback Deshaun Watson.

Browns fans didn't hold back their disdain for Watson's performance in the first half of Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, with many of them calling for second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders to replace him:

The Browns entered the locker room at halftime trailing 24-0 against the Jaguars. Their first drive ended in five plays after Watson threw an interception to Foyesade Oluokun, who returned it 22 yards to help set up Jacksonville's first touchdown. He also fumbled after taking a sack.

Watson beat out Sanders in Cleveland's quarterback competition this offseason, much to the chagrin of fans who were hoping to see the team hand the reins to the youngster. The 30-year-old missed the entire 2025 season after back-to-back Achilles surgeries, and Sunday's game marked his first regular-season start since October 2024.

Last week, Watson acknowledged that this could be his last chance to prove he could be a reliable starting quarterback in the NFL.

"Me being my last year of my deal and Year 10, I feel like this is my opportunity to be able to go and showcase that I can still play in this league," Watson said, per ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi . "I want to continue to play as well. So, this is my opportunity."

It seems like many feel Watson has already squandered his opportunity, as his first-half performance hasn't inspired much confidence that he can deliver wins for the Browns this season.

articles.title: Zay Flowers Injured, Latest on Ravens WR's Status and Fantasy Implications After 150 Yards vs. Colts
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens star receiver Zay Flowers was in the midst of a career game, but it was unfortunately cut short prematurely.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens star receiver Zay Flowers was in the midst of a career game, but it was unfortunately cut short prematurely.

Flowers dominated against the Indianapolis Colts, producing five catches for 150 yards and a touchdown in what will surely be one of the top fantasy football performances of Week 1. However, the Ravens ruled him out for the remainder of Sunday's game with a hamstring injury.

Per ESPN's Jamison Hensley , Flowers grabbed the back of his left hamstring after being tackled by Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner following a 12-yard catch in the second quarter. Hensley noted that Flowers had missed two weeks with a hamstring injury before returning to practice last week, and he entered Sunday's game without an injury designation.

Flowers did all of his damage in the first half. His 54-yard touchdown highlighted a 31-point performance by Baltimore through the first two quarters.

In addition to losing Flowers, the Ravens also lost promising rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane to a wrist injury in the first half. He made one catch for 11 yards before exiting the game. Baltimore was left with a receiving corps consisting of six-year veteran Rashod Bateman, LaJohntay Wester, who is primarily a punt returner, and Chris Moore, who was elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's opener.

Fantasy managers will certainly be hoping that Flowers won't have to miss too much time, as he showed in Sunday's first half that he can be a dependable WR1. If he's sidelined, it will be important to find a replacement on the waiver wire before Week 2.

articles.title: Jaguars Beat Browns, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Deshaun Watson, Lawrence, Judkins, Top Players
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence opened the 2026 NFL season with a massive day through the air in the Jacksonville Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Trevor Lawrence opened the 2026 NFL season with a massive day through the air in the Jacksonville Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns.

Lawrence's four-touchdown performance propelled the Jags to 1-0, while Deshaun Watson and the Browns are left looking for answers.

Three of Lawrence's four touchdown passes occurred in the first half.

Lawrence hit Parker Washington on a 30-yard touchdown pass to open the scoring.

Josh Cameron was the second recipient of a Lawrence scoring throw. That pass-and-catch produced six points from four yards out.

Lawrence then hit Brenton Strange in the second quarter to expand the advantage to 24 points before halftime.

The Jags continued the onslaught in the second half. Lawrence hit Jakobi Meyers for his fourth touchdown pass to open the third quarter scoring.

Lawrence outdueled Deshaun Watson in the all-AFC contest. Watson struggled in the first half while his Jacksonville counterpart balled out.

Watson did leave Jacksonville with one highlight, though, as he hit Denzel Boston for a 46-yard touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter.

Watson's touchdown throw came after Lawrence was already benched for the day because of the blowout on the scoreboard.

Cleveland couldn't get much offense going throughout the day. Watson was the team's leading rusher with just 38 yards.

The Browns will try to get on track in Week 2 back in Florida against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Jaguars visit the Denver Broncos next Sunday.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Climbs All-Time Rushing TD List, Who is Above Ravens RB in Record Book of NFL History?
articles.summary: The timeless Derrick Henry moved up in the NFL record book Sunday.
articles.body:
The timeless Derrick Henry moved up in the NFL record book Sunday.

The Baltimore Ravens running back scored two touchdowns on the ground in the first half of his team's season opener against the Indianapolis Colts, which gave him 124 career rushing touchdowns. He moved ahead of Marcus Allen in the process and then scored a third in the second half.

Only Emmitt Smith and LaDainian Tomlinson have more:

Henry reacted to the accomplishment after Baltimore's win over the Colts, saying "It's cool" to pass Marcus Allen while also shouting out the Ravens offensive line:

After the game, Henry also praised teammate Lamar Jackson:

Jamison Hensley of ESPN noted the two scores marked the 33rd time in his career the veteran tallied two or more touchdown runs in a game. That is the highest mark in the league since 2016.

What's more, he passed Colts legend Marvin Harrison for ninth on the NFL's all-time touchdown list with 129.

Logic dictates that at some point Henry will slow down. After all, he is 33 years old, in his 11th NFL season and led the league in rushing attempts four different times. He has surpassed 300 carries in five different seasons, including the previous two.

Yet if Sunday is any indication, there is no slowing down on the immediate horizon.

Henry's physicality makes him nearly impossible to tackle in a one-on-one scenario, but he also has the speed to get around the edge and explode for long gains.

Sharing the backfield with a mobile quarterback such as Jackson makes him even more dangerous, as defenses consistently have to pause for a second to determine which one of them has the ball. And that one second is sometimes all it takes to blow past them.

Henry will surely continue to climb the leaderboards, and he got off to quite the start this season on Sunday.

articles.title: Everything Todd Monken Said About Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Browns After Loss in HC Debut
articles.summary: Todd Monken's debut as the head coach for the Cleveland Browns was a major disappointment on Sunday.
articles.body:
Todd Monken's debut as the head coach for the Cleveland Browns was a major disappointment on Sunday.

The former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars after a subpar performance from quarterback Deshaun Watson. Given the Browns' tight quarterback race, Watson's showing will lead to questions about whether he'll remain the starter, but Monken wasn't ready to answer them on Sunday.

"I'd rather just talk about today, because I haven't had time to even look at the tape," Monken told reporters .

Watson, appearing in his first game since October 2024, threw for 205 yards, a touchdown and an interception on 16-of-22 passing. He added 38 rushing yards while being sacked five times.

Monken said he and the coaching staff will look at the tape and evaluate, but added that the loss isn't entirely on Watson.

"I'm sure as hell not firing me. I'm not firing our staff," Monken said. "I'm not giving up on all of our players... We'll evaluate everything. But to just say that emotionally here at the end — we just didn't play, didn't coach well enough."

Cleveland's defense certainly didn't make things easier on Watson and the offense. The Browns allowed Trevor Lawrence to throw for 245 yards and four touchdowns, sacking the quarterback just once.

"The obvious issues came in operation that we thought we cleaned up," Monken told reporters . "And obviously we didn't."

Watson has the veteran edge in the quarterback room, so he might have a longer leash than a younger quarterback. The Browns are also likely to understand that Watson is easing back into the swing of things after missing so much time.

But ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported before the season that the Browns feel comfortable with Shedeur Sanders stepping in under center if it comes to that, so Watson's job is anything but safe.

While things didn't go as Monken hoped in Week 1, he believes the Browns are more than capable of turning things around soon.

"I'm not down. I'm disappointed. You're not going to get me down," he told reporters . "I waited a long time to be a head coach in his league, it's freakin awesome... They better get us now because we got a good young group, we just didn't play well today."

articles.body:
Just one week into the 2026 campaign, injuries are starting to make an impact on top fantasy players.

Baltimore Ravens star Zay Flowers exited Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts with a hamstring injury, leaving his status up in the air heading into next week.

For fantasy managers potentially needing to replace Flowers, here are a handful of possible waiver-wire options.

Jalen Coker had two quiet seasons to start his career, but he looked like a completely different player in the Panthers' season opener on Sunday.

He was Bryce Young's favorite target against the Chicago Bears, recording eight receptions for 138 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The team's second-leading receiver was Tetairoa McMillan, who had five receptions for 75 yards.

The connection between Young and Coker is there, and it could lead to a breakout season for the third-year receiver. The Panthers will also face the Falcons, Browns and Lions over the next three weeks, so they aren't exactly going up against top defenses in the NFL.

Kalif Raymond isn't a new face in the NFL since he's been in the league for over a decade, but after one week, he's on pace for a career year.

In a dominant win over the Panthers, the receiver had 84 yards on eight receptions to help lead the team to a win.

While Raymond's Week 1 performance could be a fluke, all signs point to him having a solid year. He and quarterback Caleb Williams found a connection during training camp, and Raymond is well-versed in Ben Johnson's offense, having spent the last five years with the Detroit Lions.

The Bears' offense looked unstoppable in Week 1, and it seems Raymond will have plenty of balls thrown his way this season.

Devaughn Vele had just two touchdowns during the entire 2025 campaign, and he's already halfway there after Week 1.

The Saints dropped their season opener against the Lions, but their offense looked surprisingly strong as they put up 30 points in the overtime loss. Chris Olave was Tyler Shough's favorite target, but Vele collected seven receptions for 69 yards and a touchdown.

The Saints leaned on the passing game far more than the ground game on Sunday, and if that continues to be the trend, Vele could be in for a big year as the second option to Olave.

The Eagles traded for Dontayvion Wicks this offseason, hoping to add some depth with AJ Brown on his way out, but it appears Wicks might be more than an extra body.

Wicks had a solid three seasons with the Packers to start his career and found an early connection with Jaylen Hurts on Sunday, scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Washington Commanders.

DaVonta Smith might be the Eagles' WR1, but Wicks is seemingly set to be a big part of the offense this year.

articles.title: Steelers Beat Falcons, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Aaron Rodgers, Bijan, DK, Rush, Top Players
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers defeated Cooper Rush and the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 at home in Week 1 action.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers defeated Cooper Rush and the Atlanta Falcons 20-13 at home in Week 1 action.

After the game, Rodgers gave the game ball to head coach Mike McCarthy (h/t Brooke Pryor of ESPN):

"Mike's had a lot of wins, but it's always special when it's the first one at a place, and extra special when it's the team you grew up cheering for and you grew up just on the other side of the river from the facility. [His] parents are still living in town, so super special to be able to do that. I was really honestly looking forward to that today as much as anything."

Ahead of Rodgers and the Steelers' season opener, they were a 6.5-point favorite over the Falcons, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

Missed field goals, big defensive stops and utter chaos painted this Week 1 opener at Acrisure Stadium as 42-year-old Rodgers opened his 22nd NFL season with a victory.

The opening touchdown of the day belonged to the Falcons after the Steelers fumbled the ball away, setting them up in prime territory at Pittsburgh's own 25-yard line.

Rush connected with Bijan Robinson on a 23-yard touchdown pass for Atlanta's first touchdown of the 2026 season.

The Falcons returned the favor in the second, with Rush throwing an interception that resulted in a 31-yard Steelers drive down the field for their first touchdown of the season, a Rodgers connection to Pat Freiermuth.

Atlanta's Nick Folk missed a 54-yard field goal attempt in the second quarter as the Steelers entered halftime leading 13-7.

Folk's field goal woes continued in the second half, as he missed a 45-yard attempt out of the half.

Both defenses stepped up in the third, with the Falcons forcing two three-and-outs and a turnover on downs that Folk was able to turn into a successful field goal, cutting the gap to three points heading into the final frame.

Rush threw a pick-six to open the fourth quarter that veteran linebacker T.J. Watt returned for a score to give Pittsburgh a 20-10 lead.

Atlanta's Folk knocked down a 43-yard field goal to make it a one-possession game, and luckily for them, the Steelers' Chris Boswell missed a 56-yard field goal that would have put the game away.

Despite their extra chance, the Falcons only managed 11 yards, going three-and-out, while the Steelers managed to milk the clock to close out the win.

Atlanta will host the Carolina Panthers next Sunday, while Pittsburgh will hit the road to face the New England Patriots. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Reacts to Struggles in 1st Start Since 2024 as Browns Lose to Jaguars
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson was making his first start since October 2024 in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and it showed.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson was making his first start since October 2024 in Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and it showed.

Watson threw an interception on the fifth play of the game and struggled to find his footing as the Browns suffered a 34-10 loss on the road.

"We just couldn't get our rhythm back," Watson told reporters after the game. "We couldn't get drives back to help the defense. Jacksonville made plays and got points, and we didn't. I think that's where the game got away from us."

Watson finished with 205 yards, a touchdown and an interception on 16-of-22 passing. He was sacked five times as Cleveland struggled to keep up against a talented Jacksonville defense. Fans on social media quickly called out his struggles and suggested that he should be replaced by second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders.

Watson accepted responsibility for the team's disappointing offensive performance on Sunday, but he said he's looking forward to improving in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"We left a lot out there, so obviously, I'll take that responsibility full throttle," Watson told reporters . "We gotta look at the tape and see how we can be better and try to attack Tampa Bay next week to be able to get points on the board to be able to get a win."

Despite the disappointing opening to the year, Watson added that his mindset hasn't changed, and he's confident that he and the Browns will be better going forward.

"Each week is different, regardless if it would've went the other way, we would've been saying to move on from this one tomorrow after we watch the tape," Watson said .

articles.title: Bears Beat Panthers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Caleb Williams, Bryce Young, Odunze, Top Player
articles.summary: Caleb Williams led the Chicago Bears to a 59-37 victory over Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, opening their season with a winning record.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams led the Chicago Bears to a 59-37 victory over Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, opening their season with a winning record.

Despite being the home team, the Panthers were a 2.5-point underdog heading into the matchup, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

There was no defense in sight as a combined 96 points and 1,030 yards were put up in the season opener at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte.

Despite kicking off the game with a fumble for a loss, Chicago made up for it by finding the end zone twice in the first quarter. Williams ran it in for a 9-yard touchdown, and D'Andre Swift capped off a 67-yard drive with a short run up the middle to score.

Off the Bears' opening fumble, Young and the Panthers charged 42 yards downfield, capping off the drive with a 4-yard connection to Chuba Hubbard. Despite the defensive stop and early strike, Chicago led 14-7 after one quarter.

Williams connected with Cole Kmet for a 22-yard touchdown to open the second quarter. After going three-and-out on its next possession, a muffed punt was recovered by Chicago and turned into three points with a successful field goal.

Williams showed how good he is on his feet, scrambling for 29 yards to score once more.

Carolina scored on three of its five possessions, adding a deep 51-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker and a 7-yard touchdown run by Young before closing out with a field goal.

With 15 minutes left to play, the Bears led 45-31 in an insanely high-scoring Week 1 game.

Panthers' Hubbard added another score on a short, 2-yard run to tie it at 31-apiece before Chicago's Swift ran one up the middle for another score in the third, while Kyle Monangai broke loose for a 61-yard touchdown run.

Chicago began to pull away in the fourth, adding two touchdowns — a short pass to Jahdae Walker and another Swift run, his third of the day.

The Panthers opened the quarter with a fumble but found a touchdown on their next drive with another Young-Coker connection. Time ran out, and Chicago's late pullaway was too much to overcome.

Chicago will look to keep its hot offensive prowess going against the Minnesota Vikings next Sunday, while Carolina will hit the road to face the Atlanta Falcons. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kyler Murray Injured on Illegal Hit by Packers, Latest Updates on Vikings QB After Week 1 Win
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was forced to leave early in his team debut after going down with a first-quarter injury against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was forced to leave early in his team debut after going down with a first-quarter injury against the Green Bay Packers.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters after a 39-22 win over the Packers that Murray "seemed to be doing pretty well, but I wouldn't medically quote me on that."

O'Connell added Minnesota will "take it day by day."

Packers safety Javon Bullard was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play.

The Vikings announced Murray was being evaluated for a concussion before ruling him out for the rest of the game.

Carson Wentz came into the game with Murray injured, while J.J. McCarthy was inactive as the emergency quarterback. He was solid in relief, completing 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns.

Murray spent his first seven seasons with the Arizona Cardinals, who selected the former Oklahoma star and 2018 Heisman Trophy winner with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft.

The 2019 Associated Press Rookie of the Year and two-time Pro Bowler completed 67.1 percent of his passes for 20,460 yards (7.0 YPA), 121 touchdowns and 60 interceptions. He's also rushed for 3,193 yards and 32 touchdowns on 532 carries (6.0 YPC).

The 29-year-old Murray has unfortunately dealt with injuries on multiple occasions. He suffered a torn ACL in Dec. 2022 while running and making a cut against the New England Patriots. Murray missed the rest of the season and played just eight games in 2023.

Last season, Murray played only five games after suffering a foot injury against the Tennessee Titans. The Cardinals and Murray parted ways after the season, ending his seven-year tenure with the team.

Murray signed a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings in March. He joined a team looking for a veteran signal-caller after McCarthy, the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, struggled in his first season on the field in 2025 (McCarthy suffered a torn meniscus that kept him sidelined in 2024).

Though Murray and the Vikings were looking for a bounce-back year, this was not the start either were looking for against Green Bay.

Jesse Minter's first game as the head coach of the Baltimore Ravens couldn't have gone much better.

articles.title: Josh Allen torches one of NFL's best defenses to make case it's time to move on from 2025 playoff loss
articles.summary: Josh Allen passed for 334 yards, threw 2 TDs and ran for 2 others as the Buffalo Bills scored 36 points against an elite Houston Texans defense.
articles.body: Josh Allen finished last season in tears and the sight of one of the NFL's great players sobbing in the Buffalo Bills locker room after a playoff loss to the Denver Broncos led ownership to fire head coach Sean McDermott. That memory of that scene and the burden it put on Allen was buried on Sunday. Josh Allen played sensationally against the Houston Texans in a stirring 36-31 game this day. And this means stuff: It means new Bills coach Joe Brady won his head coaching debut. It means the Bills have just sent the NFL the message that they remain a Super Bowl contender for 2026 because, well, the Texans team they just beat are a Super Bowl contender. And it means Josh Allen has already joined the MVP race in earnest after he exorcised the ghosts of his horrible postseason performance and that loss which haunted all offseason. Allen also made the statement that he can indeed play up to his standard even against the Texans. "We do like Reliant Stadium, woo-hoo!" Allen exclaimed after the game. "It feels good. It feels good to start the season off right. Obviously coach Joe getting his first win as an NFL head coach ... really happy for him. [He] called a heck of a game." JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS The Texans had dominated Allen in five previous games. The Texans won four of those and limited Allen to 196 passing yards per game. Not this game. Allen played up to his billing this time. He played like he's one of the league's best players. He passed for 334 yards and two touchdowns. And he rushed for two touchdowns. Allen was in some way responsible for all four of his team's touchdowns, by either running or passing for them. Amid all those numbers, Allen tried to put the focus on others. "It's the players that we got, man," Allen said in his postgame interview with CBS. "Looking down at these stats, man, our guys made some great plays." Don't believe Allen. He delivered superstar stuff against the defense that was the NFL's best against the pass last year and was second-best in points allowed behind only the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Translation: Houston dominates on defense. And Allen dominated Houston as the Bills scored the most points that defense has allowed since 2023. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "We scored 36 points against a fantastic defense," Allen said. "However you get to 36 points in the NFL, you'll take that any other week. As long as it's more than the other guys." Allen smiling and joking after this game is quite a different snapshot than the one we got from him in his previous game – that playoff loss to the Broncos. Allen turned the ball four times in that fateful game. He fumbled twice, and threw two interceptions, including interception that set up the Broncos' game-winning drive. Allen hasn't said he lost that game for the Bills, but he has taken responsibility for it. And whether he did lose it or not, the NFL narrative that Allen couldn't get his team into the Super Bowl grew. It's impossible to make the case this was a big game on par with the playoffs. But in recording his 26th game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime – the most in the league since 2018 – Allen reminded everyone that he's over that past disappointment. And in this new season he gets another shot at the Super Bowl. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: "Saw that switch flip": Travis Kelce reveals what convinced him Patrick Mahomes is ready for his highly anticipated Chiefs comeback
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is closing in on his long-awaited return, and the Kansas City Chiefs are increasingly confident their star quarterback will be ready w.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is closing in on his long-awaited return, and the Kansas City Chiefs are increasingly confident their star quarterback will be ready when Week 1 arrives. While questions remain about how he will handle his first competitive game after major knee surgery, Travis Kelce has offered an encouraging glimpse into Mahomes’ preparation and mindset. Andy Reid’s latest update has added even more confidence around the quarterback’s comeback.Travis Kelce sees Patrick Mahomes ready for Chiefs returnMahomes has spent months working his way back after suffering ACL and LCL tears in his left knee during the Chiefs’ December loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. The injury ended his season and forced Kansas City to navigate the final stretch without its most important player.His recovery has been closely watched throughout the offseason. Mahomes did not play during the preseason, but he has remained a regular participant in Chiefs practices. For Kelce, what happened behind the scenes has been just as telling as what fans have seen on the field.Speaking on the New Heights Podcast with his brother Jason Kelce, the Chiefs tight end explained why he feels positive about Mahomes’ return.“I’m not going to tell you what I’m seeing in practice, but what I’ve seen is a guy do everything he possibly can to be ready for Week 1. What he’s done to get to this point is second to none. And you saw that switch flip when he had the surgery, how he was going to be determined to get healthy for the season,”Kelce also made it clear that Mahomes’ competitive nature has not changed during the rehabilitation process. Rather than treating the recovery as something to simply get through, the quarterback appears to have approached it with the same intensity that has defined his career.“We’re excited that he’s going to be out there rocking with us on Week 1, in terms of his ability to move around and stuff like that. He’s a competitor, man. And he only knows one way to play the game. When that ball snaps, I expect to just see Patty Mahomes out there playing football.”Andy Reid gives positive Patrick Mahomes injury updateReid has also provided an important update as the Chiefs prepare for their opener against the Denver Broncos. The coach said there is a “very good chance” Mahomes will play, provided nothing unexpected happens before the game.The Chiefs coach pointed to Mahomes’ consistency during training camp as a major reason for that confidence.“He hasn’t missed a day. You guys have seen him out there, so you know what it looks like him running around and doing his stuff. Other than having a brace on his leg, everything looks normal. He’s running around the same way he’s always done and throwing the ball like he’s always done. I think we’ll be fine there.”Still, the first real test will come under game conditions. A competitive NFL game brings pressure and contact that practice cannot fully recreate. Kansas City will therefore be watching more than just whether Mahomes can take the field.The Chiefs have plenty riding on his return. His absence last season coincided with a late collapse that saw Kansas City lose its final three games and miss the playoffs for the first time since 2014.For now, though, the signs are encouraging. articles.title: Instant Report Card Grades for Bills' NFL Week 1 Game vs. Texans
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are 1-0.
articles.body:
For much of the afternoon, it didn't feel as though we'd be writing that.

With the defense struggling in a demanding road opener against a tough Houston Texans team, Buffalo found itself in a classic back-and-forth bout that felt uncomfortably familiar for fans accustomed to heartbreak in chaotic finishes. But this time, the Bills held on for a 36-31 victory.

Buffalo now prepares to unveil its brand-new stadium to the world Thursday night against Detroit. Before turning the page, here is our report card from the opener.

Allen is the best quarterback in the world right now, and he practically carried the Bills to this victory in his first game as a 30-year-old.

The preseason MVP favorite averaged a comically high 11.5 yards per attempt and was lights-out over and over again on deep and intermediate tosses to Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, and—in the biggest of spots—Joshua Palmer.

He generated a combined four passing and rushing touchdowns and didn't turn the ball over—although he did nearly fumble in a key fourth-quarter moment and was almost intercepted twice in and around the Houston end zone.

That's about all there is to keep this from being an A+ for Allen.

The reigning rushing champion broke free for 20 yards combined on his first two carries but was hardly a factor from there, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry on 11 attempts the remainder of the game.

He gets credit for a pivotal 12-yard run to launch what turned into the game-winning drive deep inside Buffalo territory, but it's worth noting that he fumbled at the end of that play and was saved by teammate O'Cyrus Torrence's recovery.

It was a good-not-great performance, albeit against a killer defense that seemed to adjust well after Cook's strong start.

Folks might have been wondering where Moore was hiding when the veteran newcomer was held without a catch (or a target) until late in the first half. The reality? He was opening things up for the rest of the offense while being frequently double-teamed by one of the most talented secondaries in the NFL.

And he eventually delivered in a huge way with 100 yards and a sweet touchdown, while also drawing two pass interference penalties (the first of which occurred in the end zone on a deep ball, leading directly to a score).

Shakir was once again Mr. Reliable for Allen, well before Moore and Kincaid became bigger factors as the game wore on. He set the tone early for the offense with a pair of key first-half catches, as well as a strong run on a lateral to set up a fourth-and-short.

Depth receivers aren't always going to factor in against defenses like Houston's, but you'd hope to see more from Coleman than a single catch. Technically it was only a one-yard reception, but the lateral to Shakir was well executed.

It was immediately unclear whether Palmer or Allen erred on a fourth-quarter play that nearly resulted in an interception in the end zone. Regardless, the 26-year-old made up for it all with a 34-yard touchdown catch on the very next play. That was ultimately the dagger.

Beast! Five catches on six targets for 130 yards from Kincaid, who gained more than 30 yards on three of those receptions. No tight end in the NFL had more than five 30-plus-yard catches in the entire 2025 season, yet Kincaid just did it in one game. If the 26-year-old former first-round pick can stay healthy, he could have a legendary breakout season.

Just a single seven-yard catch but no drops or obvious mistakes for the veteran, although he gets extra credit for helping bulldoze Allen into the end zone on his long touchdown scramble.

The tackles get props for the fact the line surrendered just two sacks against such a fierce defensive front, but Dawkins whiffed on a critical fourth-down block and had a few other sloppy reps.

The new starter at left guard experienced some tough downs, giving up a sack, drawing a holding penalty, and surrendering a hit on Allen that could have easily resulted in a hand injury.

It was a sloppier-than-usual showing from the 28-year-old vet, and this entire unit. That said, McGovern and Co. were routinely schemed into tough spots by Joe Brady and Pete Carmichael.

Ditto for Torrence, but he deserves major credit for a heads-up play and exemplary hustle on that game-saving fumble recovery.

Also far from perfect, but his only costly mistake came on a one-on-one defeat against Danielle Hunter on a key third-down play. That's not bad considering the competition.

Unfortunately, the Bills' new high-priced pass-rusher was missing in action for much of the afternoon. He wound up with a few hurries but also took some bad angles that resulted in extra yardage on rushes and straight-up missed several tackles.

Fortunately, Rousseau compensated for that with a sick performance that included two strip sacks, five quarterback hits and—in his debut as an outside linebacker—a superb pass breakup in coverage that kept Houston buried near its own goal line in the second half. It was one of the best games of his career.

The second-year fourth-round pick made some monster plays to set the tone. Without Rousseau and Walker, this D might have surrendered 50. The Bills might have found a budding star here. Walker seems to rise up in big situations.

The splashy plays mainly belonged to Rousseau and Walker, but Oliver was quite effective as a pass rusher and singlehandedly drew a holding penalty on Houston in a key fourth-quarter spot.

Playing an increased role because T.J. Sanders was out, Jackson was frequently pushed around in the trenches. But he was never embarrassed and he did make a great stop to set the tone on the first play of a three-and-out to start the second half.

It was a roller-coaster performance from Bernard. He made several nice stops in important situations in the first half and was extremely active overall but also appeared to be totally out of place when Jaylin Noel broke free on a busted coverage for 35 yards late in the first half and struggled consistently on a long Houston drive in the middle of the second quarter.

Williams looked out of place far too often, was burned by poor angles on multiple plays and often failed to close out plays without needing extra help. He was useless in coverage.

It was a tough assignment with Nico Collins one-on-one most of the day, and Benford struggled quite a bit in coverage while also missing some tackles. The Bills quite simply need more from him as the top cover guy. He avoids an F because he came up big with consecutive impressive wrap-ups on Collins inside the sticks to hold Houston to a long field goal in the fourth quarter.

It's rarely a bad sign when you hardly see anything from a corner for four quarters. There was a weird mixup with Dee Alford that could have easily cost them the game but my initial impression is that it was more on Alford than Hairston.

In addition to that mixup above, the offseason acquisition was often inadequate in coverage—especially on a big 20-yard Xavier Hutchinson third-down conversion in the fourth quarter.

The veteran was in on a lot of plays, and it showed with those eight tackles. But he did miss a couple as well, and he failed to make any impact plays.

The promising sophomore was the lone bright spot in the secondary. Bishop's importance was highlighted when he briefly exited with an injury midway through the game and the secondary went from bad to embarrassing with Damar Hamlin on the field.

There's been some concern here, but you can't complain about a 6-for-6 day (three field goals, three extra points).

A 54.5 average on two punts is a hell of a way to start your career.

A fantastic kick return from Dortch set up Buffalo's first touchdown of the season, and he was effective on both of his punt returns.

articles.title: "A huge void in his life": Tom Brady’s father worried about the NFL legend’s life after retirement and split from Gisele Bündchen
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady’s retirement from the NFL was never going to be an ordinary goodbye. When the seven-time Super Bowl champion finally stepped away in Februar.
articles.body: Tom Brady’s retirement from the NFL was never going to be an ordinary goodbye. When the seven-time Super Bowl champion finally stepped away in February 2023, attention quickly turned to what life would look like without the game that had shaped nearly his entire adult life. Around that time, Brady’s father shared a revealing concern: the quarterback might struggle to replace the purpose, routine and intensity that football had given him for more than two decades.Tom Brady’s father worried about life after retirementIn a February 2023 report, Brady Sr. opened up about the challenge his son faced after ending his playing career. The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback had spent 23 seasons living by the demands of professional football.For Brady, the game was much more than a job. It provided a strict routine, constant competition and a close bond with teammates. Walking away meant losing all of those things at once.Speaking recently to The Atlantic, Tom Brady Sr. remarked how his son, who hung up his cleats “for good” earlier this month after 23 seasons “is going to have a huge void in his life.”“… Nothing will ever replace the joy Tommy had playing in football games, hanging with teammates, and joshing around in the locker room,” the elder Brady said.“Somehow he’s going to have to find a substitute for that, just like every other guy has.”His comments offered a glimpse into a side of retirement that often gets overlooked. Athletes can spend years preparing their bodies for the end of their careers, but finding a new sense of purpose can be just as demanding.Those close to Brady had reportedly worried about the transition because of how deeply he had invested himself in football. His work ethic became one of the defining parts of his remarkable career.Tom Brady retirement fears were rooted in his love for footballThe concern was not entirely new. Years before his final retirement, Brady himself admitted that the end of his playing days made him uneasy.During a 2021 appearance on Hodinkee Radio, Brady spoke openly about the uncertainty surrounding life after football.“I think there’s a lot of time and energy still focused on being a great quarterback, that when that’s done, although I’m a little fearful of it ending, I am open to the belief that there will be a lot of opportunities for me to do things that I haven’t had a chance to do that I really think I can help a lot of people,” Brady said at time.There was also an unforgettable story from his father that highlighted just how difficult it had always been for Brady to switch off from football.Former NFL receiver Cris Carter recalled meeting Brady Sr. before his son’s seventh Super Bowl victory in 2021. According to Carter, Brady’s father was less concerned about the game itself than whether his son would ever know when to stop.“The night before the game, I happen to meet up with Tom Brady’s dad and asked him what he thought about the game, the opportunity to win again,” Carter said. “He said the only thing he’s worried about is the kid, the kid won’t go home. He said ‘the kid is outside still playing, and he won’t come in. It’s raining, everything.’ He said, ‘I am only afraid the kid won’t stop playing even if he wins.’”Ultimately, Brady entered retirement with a new set of priorities. His children, business interests and future broadcasting career offered different ways to fill the space football had occupied.The story, published in 2023, remains an interesting look at the personal challenge behind one of the biggest retirements in NFL history. For a player who spent 23 years chasing excellence, learning how to stop may have been his toughest challenge yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "What's the point of a married dude bringing up an ex": Aaron Rodgers’ Shailene Woodley revelations spark backlash from people close to the actress
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers has reopened an old chapter of his personal life, and the reaction has been swift. During a recent podcast appearance, the Pittsburgh St.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has reopened an old chapter of his personal life, and the reaction has been swift. During a recent podcast appearance, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback spoke in detail about his former relationship with Shailene Woodley, including their engagement and breakup. People close to the actress reportedly questioned why Rodgers chose to revisit a relationship that ended years ago, especially after Woodley had previously explained how difficult that period was for her.Aaron Rodgers’ comments about Shailene Woodley draw backlashRodgers discussed Woodley during an appearance on Cam Heyward’s “Not Just Football” podcast, released on September 10, 2026. The former couple became engaged in December 2020, but their relationship unraveled within months.According to Rodgers, he proposed and Woodley accepted. He later claimed that she told him only days after the proposal that she needed to deal with another man before they could marry.Rodgers also recalled seeing signs that their engagement was falling apart. He said Woodley had removed her engagement ring by March 2021. Although the pair attempted to repair their relationship later that year, Rodgers said the effort ultimately failed.He claimed Woodley eventually told him, “I don't want to be with you.”The comments have reportedly frustrated people in Woodley’s circle. Sources cited by TMZ said the actress has always preferred to keep her personal relationships away from public attention.One source questioned Rodgers’ decision to bring up the relationship at all."What's the point of a married dude bringing up an ex he hasn't spoken with in over 2 years?"Rodgers, who is now married, also pushed back against the idea that he was responsible for damaging Woodley’s life.“Shai, you left me, you took the ring off. What are we talking about regarding me ruining your life?”His decision to revisit the relationship comes despite Woodley previously explaining why she rarely discusses their breakup.Shailene Woodley previously described a painful periodWoodley spoke about Rodgers and the end of their relationship in a December 2024 interview with Outside magazine. Rather than offering a detailed account, she explained that discussing the romance remained emotionally difficult."I haven't shared much about my relationship with Aaron because it always makes me cry," she said.Woodley also described the relationship in a way that captured its complexity without reducing it to a simple success or failure."It was not right. But it was beautiful," she said.She then opened up about a deeply difficult period in early 2022, around the time the breakup became public."I had a really awful, traumatic thing happen in early 2022," she said. "I felt like I lost my soul, my self, my happiness, my joy. I really understood depression and anxiety and, like, complete soul detachment."Woodley said her depression became so severe that even looking at a tree could leave her feeling nothing. Support from her close friend and stylist Kris Zero helped her begin moving forward. Surfing, working at a ranch and spending time outdoors became part of that process.Rodgers also addressed another famous former relationship during the same podcast appearance. He disputed Danica Patrick’s past description of their breakup and said their relationship had deteriorated over time."She had just retired," Rodgers said. "She was depressed and not fun to be around, but I didn't leave her because I was trying to be there and be a good partner."Rodgers further acknowledged that he had been “emotionally unavailable” during his relationships with Patrick and Woodley because of unresolved feelings connected to his now-wife, Brittani.For now, his comments have brought renewed attention to relationships both sides had seemingly left behind. The discussion also highlights how differently former partners can remember the same chapter of their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Jason and Kylie Kelce built a $6 million estate, bought a $2.2 million beach house and embraced luxury
articles.summary: NFL News: Jason and Kylie Kelce have turned NFL success into a lifestyle that extends far beyond the football field. Their wealth has grown through Jason’s play.
articles.body: Jason and Kylie Kelce have turned NFL success into a lifestyle that extends far beyond the football field. Their wealth has grown through Jason’s playing career, major media deals, business investments and their own podcast ventures. Today, the couple’s spending reflects both sides of their lives: a comfortable family home, expensive hobbies, valuable real estate and business moves that continue to expand the Kelce brand.Jason and Kylie Kelce’s lavish Pennsylvania estateJason Kelce entered the NFL in 2011 with a contract worth about $2.1 million. By the final year of his career, his annual deal had climbed to $14 million. His NFL contracts are estimated to have brought in around $88 million before accounting for endorsement income.Retirement did not slow the money-making side of his career. His “New Heights” podcast with brother Travis Kelce became a major success, eventually leading to a reported $100 million deal with Amazon’s Wondery in 2024.Kylie Kelce has built her own media presence through “Not Gonna Lie,” which quickly became one of the biggest podcasts on Spotify and Apple Podcasts after its 2024 launch.Jason summed up the family’s growing profile during a 2024 appearance on “Golfer's Journal.”“I think the Kelce brand, in general, is pretty high right now.”He added, “I don't know that it should be this high. If anything, we're the overdog now. We're way overvalued, probably.”The couple’s real estate choices certainly match that success. They initially purchased a four-bedroom home in Haverford, Pennsylvania, for $680,000 after negotiating $120,000 off the asking price. As their family expanded, they bought the neighboring eight-acre property for $3.96 million in 2020.In 2023, they added another adjoining property for $1.35 million. The goal was reportedly to combine the properties into one large private estate. By 2025, the family was seeking approval for further expansion and additional security measures.Their real estate portfolio also includes a $2.2 million beach house in Sea Isle City, New Jersey. The three-story property has four bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms and multiple family spaces.Jason Kelce’s hobbies and family spending add to the luxuryThe Kelces also spend heavily on the things they enjoy. Jason reportedly created a dedicated man cave filled with sports memorabilia and rare collectibles. He has also spent around $2,000 a month building a vintage book collection.His business interests have grown alongside those hobbies. Jason and Travis became significant owners and operators of Garage Beer in 2024. Jason later appeared in a major Super Bowl commercial for the brand in 2026, adding another high-profile moment to the brothers’ growing business portfolio.Golf has also become more than a pastime for Jason. In 2025, he took an ownership role in Sullivan County Golf and Country Club in New York.Family experiences come with their own price tag. Kylie once revealed that the couple bought 13 additional tickets for the 2023 Super Bowl, costing about $52,000 in total.Their children’s comfort is another priority. During a Pottery Barn Kids collaboration, Kylie explained the thinking behind their playroom.“Family is everything. It's really important to have this space feel cozy and comfortable.”From property and podcasts to golf, collectibles and family experiences, Jason and Kylie Kelce have built a lifestyle that reflects how dramatically their fortunes have changed. What began with an NFL contract has grown into a much broader family brand, giving the Kelces plenty of ways to turn their success into long-term wealth.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chargers let down almost one-third of survival pool players with huge upset loss to Cardinals
articles.summary: The Chargers were big favorites in their season opener vs. Arizona.
articles.body:
The pick for NFL survival pools seemed so easy for Week 1. The Los Angeles Chargers were the biggest favorite on the board, one of the biggest opening-game favorites over many years .

And now, the Chargers go down in infamy as one of the popular survival picks that got people eliminated before the theme song for the first "Sunday Night Football" of the season hit.

The Chargers, the most popular pick at Yahoo Survival Football for Week 1 as they were picked by 32.5%, are 0-1. The Arizona Cardinals , who closed as a 9.5-point underdog at most sportsbooks, pulled a huge upset by beating the Chargers 26-14.

The Chargers couldn't get a stop early. The Cardinals' first five possessions resulted in a touchdown, three field goals and a missed field goal. A lot was made this offseason about the Chargers hiring Mike McDaniel to be their offensive coordinator. Perhaps not enough was made of Los Angeles losing defensive coordinator Jesse Minter to the Baltimore Ravens ' head-coaching job.

The Chargers were still barely trailing in the fourth quarter when their special teams had a massive mistake. The Cardinals blocked a punt and took over at the Chargers' 3-yard line. Arizona scored a touchdown two plays later, turning a 16-14 lead into 23-14 with 11:44 to play.

There was still time after that, even trailing by two possessions, but Justin Herbert threw deep with two defenders in coverage, and it was picked off by safety Andrew Wingard .

The Chargers went away quietly after that. Los Angeles got a lot of offseason hype, which has happened in plenty of recent offseasons, only to see the Chargers disappoint everyone. It's just one game but Sunday was a big warning that the Chargers might be going down that same road again.

Survival pickers won't be forgiving them anytime soon.

The Arizona Cardinals pulled off the biggest upset of Week 1 after they downed the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 on Sunday.

The Chargers came into the game as 8.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but the rebuilding Cardinals got their season started off right with a big win over a team looking to compete for a Super Bowl.

Jacoby Brissett spent his offseason trying to convince the Cardinals he was worth starting quarterback money, and he proved early on that he had a strong argument.

He led Arizona down the field on its first offensive drive, and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love found the end zone for his first NFL touchdown.

The Chargers answered on the following drive as Omarion Hampton took one in from eight yards out on a tough run.

The second quarter was filled with errors from the Chargers, as they had a fumble that led to a field goal for the Cardinals before turning it over on downs on their next drive. Arizona went into halftime leading by six.

After a field goal put the Cardinals up 16-7, a defensive pass interference helped set up a touchdown for the Chargers on a catch from Ladd McConkey.

Mistakes mounted again in the fourth quarter for the Chargers. A blocked punt set up a touchdown for the Cardinals, and Justin Herbert threw an interception on the following drive.

After the Chargers turned it over on downs again, the Cardinals notched a field goal to make it a 26-14 game with just over two minutes to play, and that sealed the deal.

Arizona perhaps wasn't viewed as a playoff team coming into the season, but the Cardinals certainly looked the part in Mike LaFleur's first game as head coach.

Meanwhile, the Chargers have some reflecting to do after the early-season upset.

articles.title: Raiders Beat Dolphins, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Kirk Cousins, Malik Willis, Top Players
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins led the Las Vegas Raiders to a 27-13 home win over Malik Willis and the Miami Dolphins to open the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins led the Las Vegas Raiders to a 27-13 home win over Malik Willis and the Miami Dolphins to open the 2026 NFL season.

The veteran-led Raiders entered their matchup as a 3-point favorite over Miami ahead of Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

In his 15th season under center, Cousins is showing no signs of slowing down in his first year in Sin City alongside second-year player Ashton Jeanty, with the duo leading the team to 290 total yards (130 rushing).

After eight plays, the Dolphins punted the ball away in the first, allowing the Raiders to eat up the clock with a nearly nine-minute possession that resulted in a Cousins connection to Jack Bech for six points.

Miami added a pair of field goals in the second, attempting to chip away at the Raiders' lead, while Las Vegas registered a field goal of its own and another touchdown, this time on a 13-yard Cousins pass to Ashton Jeanty.

The Raiders' first miscue came out of the break when Cousins threw an interception, setting up a 52-yard, four play drive for Willis and the Dolphins to find the end zone for the first time on the day. Willis ran one in on a 14-yard run, cutting the deficit to four.

Las Vegas quickly responded on another Cousins-Jeanty connection, adding a field goal on offense and an interception on defense, while Miami missed a field goal to close out the third, trailing 27-13.

Despite some fourth-quarter struggles, including a three-and-out drive and near-costly interception by the Raiders, Miami was unable to put together any offense, and Las Vegas walked away with a Week 1 win.

Both teams will head west next Sunday — Las Vegas to face the Los Angeles Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET and Miami to take on the San Francisco 49ers at 5:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Stefon Diggs penalized for celebration after first TD with Commanders, ruining 2-point conversion shot in loss to Eagles
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs wrapped himself around the field goal post after scoring a touchdown on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
Stefon Diggs got a little too excited for his first touchdown with the Washington Commanders .

Diggs caught a perfect 10-yard pass from Jayden Daniels for an easy touchdown early in the fourth quarter of their 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon. That brought them back within two points of the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field, too, and just a conversion away from tying the game back up at a critical point of the contest.

But before they could even attempt it, Diggs ruined the opportunity.

Immediately after catching the ball in the end zone, Diggs wrapped himself around the field goal post to celebrate the score. That drew a quick unsportsmanlike conduct penalty from the officials, and forced the Commanders to kick the extra point instead.

While there was no guarantee that the Commanders were going to tie the game, Diggs' excessive celebration backed them up 15 yards and ensured that they wouldn't get the chance.

"As soon as I wrapped my arms around it, I was like … 'Oh, I forgot.' It's not back in the day," Diggs said, via NBC4's JP Finlay . "I've been playing for a long time. You used to [be able to] do that … I've got to be better."

Diggs signed a one-year, $12 million deal to join the Commanders last month in a move meant to boost Washington's receiver room. Diggs had 1,013 yards and four touchdowns last season with the New England Patriots . The Commanders mark the fourth team that Diggs has played for now in as many years. His touchdown grab was his third catch of the game.

The Eagles responded with a 43-yard touchdown pass to tight end Dallas Goedert after Diggs' penalty, so they took control of the game right back instantly and made it far less meaningful.

The Commanders managed to get down into scoring position, and then Daniels found Antonio Williams for a touchdown inside the two-minute warning. But they were still down by two.

And the two-point conversion attempt failed. Daniels tried to dump it off to John Bates , but the Eagles stopped him short.

The loss is not on Diggs, and the Eagles defense made a great play at the end of the game to seal the deal. But still, had it been a tie game before Goedert's touchdown, the final stretch of the contest in Philadelphia could have absolutely played out differently.
