articles.title: Fantasy football waiver wire Week 2: 10 players to pick up
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers will be looking to replace several injured starters ahead of Week 2. Here are some of the top waiver write targets.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers got a first taste of their teams during Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Many were happy with what they saw, especially during what became a high-scoring first NFL Sunday of the season.

Several NFL teams had elite offensive performances to open the season. The Chicago Bears paced the field with 59 points, but eight other teams were able to open their seasons with 30-point performances ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

What type of impact will those top-tier performances have on the waiver wire? Many of the top performers from Week 1 were already rostered across a majority of fantasy football leagues, but there are still a handful of quality options across positions fantasy managers can target to improve their rosters and help replace injured playmakers.

Here's a look at the best players to target on the waiver wire ahead of fantasy football Week 2, from a rookie running back with a solid-looking role to a receiver in a big role who flew under the radar entering the 2026 NFL season.

NFL Week 1 reactions after wins, big moments and breakout performances

Week 2 fantasy football waiver wire targets

RB Kaelon Black , San Francisco 49ers (Rostered in 26% of Yahoo leagues)

Christian McCaffrey has long been the 49ers' workhorse, but Kyle Shanahan showed a willingness to lighten the veteran's load against the Rams . McCaffrey and Black, a third-round rookie, each handled 15 touches in San Francisco 's 27-7 win in Australia.

Notably, Black handled 14 carries to McCaffrey's 10, and the split wasn't limited to the latter stages of the blowout. Black was out-carrying McCaffrey 7-3 at halftime , so if that split continues, the Indiana product could end up being a solid flex play moving forward.

WR Dontayvion Wicks , Philadelphia Eagles (Rostered in 15% of Yahoo leagues)

The Eagles had a massive target void to fill after trading A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots . Makai Lemon was expected to take on a large portion of those targets, but instead, Wicks emerged as Jalen Hurts ' preferred secondary wideout target.

Wicks racked up two catches for 73 yards and a touchdown while seeing four targets, third-most on the team behind DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert . He looked good as a field-stretching option, and if Hurts and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion continue to trust him, he could have flex potential across fantasy formats.

QB Bryce Young , Carolina Panthers (Rostered in 13% of Yahoo leagues)

Many were expecting the Panthers' defense to take a step forward in 2026. Instead, they surrendered a whopping 59 points in their season opener against the Bears, but Young did a nice job keeping his team in the game.

Young racked up 361 passing yards and three passing touchdowns while adding a score and 10 yards on the ground. His production wasn't limited to garbage time – only one of his touchdowns came with his team down by more than one possession in the second half – and his continued improvement as a downfield passer could allow him to develop into a quality streamer.

Young is playing the Falcons in Week 2, so if you're looking for a flier at quarterback, he could be worth a shot. Also, if wide receiver Jalen Coker is available in your league, feel free to grab him. He's 60% rostered in Yahoo leagues, but that number should rise considerably after he logged eight catches for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1.

QB Tyler Shough , New Orleans Saints (Rostered in 40% of Yahoo leagues)

Shough got off to a bad start in the Saints ' Week 1 loss to the Lions, but he bounced back nicely in the second half. He led New Orleans to 24 points over the final 20 minutes of regulation and posted 410 passing yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions during the overtime loss.

Shough attempted 56 passes, and that type of week-to-week volume could make him a quality streamer. Add in that he plays in the ever-weak NFC South and scooping him up could be a worthwhile move for fantasy managers needing quarterback depth.

WR Devaughn Vele , New Orleans Saints (Rostered in 6% of Yahoo leagues)

Unsurprisingly, Chris Olave was Shough's clear-cut No. 1 target against the Lions. That said, Vele ranked second on the team in targets with nine and turned them into seven receptions, 69 yards and a touchdown.

Vele showed good hands throughout the contest and made a couple of nifty, diving catches. That should instill confidence in the veteran as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver, at least until Jordyn Tyson returns, so he will have flex appeal if the Saints continue to be a high-volume passing offense.

WR Kalif Raymond , Chicago Bears (Rostered in 0% of Yahoo leagues)

Many spent the summer debating whether Luther Burden III , Rome Odunze or Colston Loveland would be the top target in Chicago's offense. But in Week 1, it was Raymond who paced the Bears' pass-catching weapons in opportunities.

Raymond led the Bears in targets (9), receptions (8) and receiving yards (84). It wasn't just because of the Bears' blowout, either. He often shook free because the Panthers focused on limiting Burden, Odunze and Loveland while also containing Caleb Williams .

Bears coach Ben Johnson has expressed a desire to blow out his opponents in 2026, so that could give Raymond flex appeal if he keeps getting targets. He's certainly worth stashing, given what Chicago showed it is capable of offensively in Week 1.

WR Caleb Douglas , Miami Dolphins (Rostered in 11% of Yahoo leagues)

The Dolphins are likely to play from behind a lot in 2026, so Malik Willis ' preferred target was always going to be of interest for fantasy managers. Douglas posted a team-high five receptions for 94 yards in the team's 27-13 loss to the Raiders , making him the early favorite as a breakout player in Miami.

WR Rashod Bateman , Baltimore Ravens (Rostered in 2% of Yahoo leagues)

There's nothing sexy about picking up Bateman, especially after he failed to make a catch in the Ravens' season-opening win against the Colts . But Baltimore lost Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) to injuries against Indianapolis , and Lamar Jackson will have to throw to somebody moving forward.

Bateman is the most experienced option in Baltimore's receiver room, so he's worth stashing as a potential matchup-based flex play.

TE Pat Freiermuth , Pittsburgh Steelers (Rostered in 6% of Yahoo leagues)

Freiermuth only saw 54 targets during the 2025 NFL season, his second-fewest in a campaign across his five-season NFL career, while battling Jonnu Smith and Darnell Washington for playing time.

Mike McCarthy seems more willing than previous offensive coordinator Arthur Smith to trust Freiermuth as his top tight end. Freiermuth rewarded that faith by catching all five of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown, and he should continue to be a quality middle-of-the-field threat with Aaron Rodgers still largely preferring to throw the ball within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage.

TE Mike Gesicki , Cincinnati Bengals (Rostered in 1% of Yahoo leagues)

Gesicki led the Bengals in targets (7) and receiving yards (78) against the Buccaneers while catching Joe Burrow 's lone touchdown pass. If opposing defenses continue to focus on limiting Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , that should open space in which Gesicki can operate over the middle of the field.

articles.title: Browns Get Bad News on Injured RB Dylan Sampson After Loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns got a negative update on injured running back Dylan Sampson following the team's loss to Jacksonville. The post Browns Get Bad News on I...
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars mopped the Cleveland Browns by a score of 34-10 in the season opener, and the news got even worse after the game was over.

Running back Dylan Sampson , a second-year player with a knack for making dynamic plays out of the backfield in the pass game, left the contest early in the first half with a knee injury.

And while it will likely be Monday before the team confirms the precise nature of Sampson's issue, reports out of the visitor's locker room in Jacksonville were more than a little discouraging.

"#Browns Dylan Sampson on crutches after game, brace on left knee," Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported via X on Sunday, September 13.

Sampson, a fourth-round pick in 2025, tallied 65 rushing attempts for 175 yards during his rookie campaign. He added 33 catches for 271 yards and two scores on 40 targets in the pass game.

Browns Struggled to Establish Run Game in Season Opener Against Jaguars

The ground game in general was a disaster for Cleveland on Sunday, as quarterback Deshaun Watson led the way with six carries for 38 yards.

Starter Quinshon Judkins , who played his first regular season football since fracturing his right fibula and dislocating his ankle late last year, logged 12 attempts and gained just 33 yards. He added two catches for 17 yards through the air.

Rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion added three carries for 15 yards, while Raheim Sanders added one rushing attempt for a single yard.

The Browns finished the day with 87 yards on 22 carries for an average of 4.0 yards per rush.

Raheim Sanders Likely to Replace Dylan Sampson as RB2 Based on Seriousness of Injury

Sanders, an undrafted rookie in 2025 out of South Carolina, will step into the RB2 role behind Judkins if Sampson's injury is serious enough to sideline him for any portion of time, which Cabot's visual report indicates it is.

Sanders appeared in four games for the Browns last season, earning a single start. He tallied 27 rushes for 92 yards and one TD , adding three catches for 21 yards on four targets.

Browns first-year head coach Todd Monken also showed an affinity for using Concepcion in certain run concepts, which is something Browns fans can likely expect to see more of as the team tries to get the football into the explosive first-round playmaker's hands as often as possible.

articles.title: Caleb Williams and Bears trounce Panthers 59-37 in highest-scoring season opener in NFL history
articles.summary: Ben Johnson said he slept well Saturday night at the Bears’ team hotel, sensing that quarterback Caleb Williams was more than ready for the season opener.
articles.body:
Ben Johnson said he slept well Saturday night at the Bears ' team hotel, sensing that quarterback Caleb Williams was more than ready for the season opener.

Williams, the No. 1 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, looked like a league MVP candidate on Sunday, throwing for 269 yards and two touchdowns and running for 65 yards and two more scores as the Bears trounced the Carolina Panthers 59-37 in the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history.

"I could kind of tell (Saturday) night when we did our quarterback meeting one last time that he was just on top of it," Johnson said. "Everything he was rattling out, like where my eyes need to be and what I'm thinking. ... So I went to bed and just slept really well."

Johnson's prolific Bears broke a franchise record for points in an opener, a mark that had stood since 1948, when Chicago hung 45 points on Green Bay at Wrigley Field.

The 59 points were the most allowed by the Panthers since they began play as an expansion team in 1995.

D'Andre Swift, who received a $33.75 million contract extension earlier this week, paid immediate dividends for the Bears, rushing for 124 yards on 18 carries with three touchdowns, while Kyle Monangai had 100 yards on the ground, including a 61-yard touchdown burst in the second half.

"He's had a good week, huh?" Johnson said of Swift. "He earned (the contract), every step of it. We really value what he brings to the table. He has had a great spring and I don't think anybody in our camp is surprised he is out of the gate in strong fashion."

It was the fourth-most points in Bears history. The most came in their notorious 73-0 win over Washington in the 1940 NFL title game.

"That's how we want to look each week," Williams said. "That's who we want to be each week."

Chicago and Carolina scored eight more points than the previous record of 88 set in Tampa Bay's 48-40 win over New Orleans in 2018.

Although Carolina's Bryce Young fell to 0-4 in openers, it was by far the best season debut of his career. The 2023 No. 1 overall pick threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran for a score.

Jalen Coker , who emerged as Carolina's No. 2 receiver last year, had eight catches for a career-high 138 yards and two TDs.

But the Panthers were done in three turnovers — a muffed punt by Jimmy Horn, a fumble by Tetairoa McMillan fumble and a pick by Young — and a leaky defense that committed untimely penalties.

The Bears put up 552 yards on offense and had 26 first downs. They were 10 of 14 on third-down conversions.

"It was an incredible day by the Bears," Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "There were some things that we did to give a really good offense more opportunities. They don't need any more opportunities. They were already creating their own."

The Bears turned the ball over on their first possession, but quickly recovered and scored seven touchdowns on their next 12 drives, including the final four possessions to close the game.

Williams showed pure command, completing several pinpoint passes while racking up 196 yards through the air in the first half, including a perfectly placed 22-yard touchdown strike to Cole Kmet .

"He couldn't have put ball in a better spot and Cole made a heck of a catch there, too," Johnson said.

He also showed the elusiveness that makes him hard to contain. He ran for 52 yards and two TDs — including a 29-yard scamper — before the break as the Bears took a 31-24 lead into the locker room.

Bears shrug off a fourth-down try that went wrong

Chicago's lead might have been bigger had it not been for a questionable decision by Johnson.

With the Bears leading 21-14, Johnson went for it on fourth-and-1 at the Chicago 21, but Williams came up short on a QB sneak.

"I felt pretty about the call," Johnson said.

In the end, it didn't matter. Mistakes ended the Panthers' hopes in the second half.

After Chuba Hubbard scored his second TD to tie the game at 31-all, Carolina defensive end Derrick Brown was flagged for a late hit on Williams, allowing a drive to continue. That led to Swift's 1-yard TD run.

The Panthers went for it on fourth down near midfield on their next possession but Young couldn't connect with McMillan on a lofted pass down the left sideline. Chicago cashed in on the next play as Monangai broke through a hole in the middle and raced 61 yards for a 45-31 lead — a play that Williams called his favorite of the game.

"That's a crushing thing when you're in that situation when you are midfield and you get a downhill run like that," Williams said.

On Carolina's next drive, McMillan fumbled, giving the Bears the ball back. Williams cashed in with a scoring strike to a wide-open Jahdea Walker for a 52-31 lead with 6:27 remaining.

Bears: LT Braxton Jones left late in the third quarter with an upper-body injury. CB Tyrique Stevenson injured his shoulder. Neither appeared to be serious.

Panthers: DT Bobby Brown left in the second half with a back injury.

articles.title: Vikings Beat Packers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Love, Jefferson, Top Players as Kyler Injured
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota Vikings worked their way to a Week 1 39-22 comeback victory over Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota Vikings worked their way to a Week 1 39-22 comeback victory over Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

The home team was listed as the narrow 1.5-favorite ahead of the matchup, per FanDuel Sportsbook with a new quarterback under center in Minnesota.

In Kyler Murray's Minnesota Vikings debut, he was forced out early after an illegal hit by Packers safety Javon Bullard sent him to the locker room in the first quarter.

The Vikings announced that Murray was being evaluated for a concussion before he was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Murray spent his first seven years in the league with the Arizona Cardinals.

After Murray went down, 11-year veteran quarterback Carson Wentz stepped in, leading the Vikings back from a 22-10 deficit with just over five minutes left in the third quarter.

Murray's first throw in purple and gold was not what he hoped for, as he threw an interception that was returned 11 yards and set up Green Bay for a field goal.

Love added to the score with an 81-yard bomb to Christian Watson before Minnesota added a field goal to close out the quarter. Green Bay led 9-3 after 15 minutes.

Despite an opening field goal from Green Bay in the second, neither offense could get it going.

Minnesota was the first to convert with just under two minutes remaining, with Wentz finding Jefferson on a 39-yard pass for six.

Love and Green Bay marched down the field with an efficient 1:41 drive, Love finding Watson once more for a score to stretch the lead to 19-10 before halftime.

Green Bay added a field goal, but Minnesota was the lone team to find the end zone out of the break, with Wentz finding T.J. Hockenson with a 16-yard connection to the finish line, closing the gap 22-17.

The Vikings put the hammer down in the fourth on both sides of the ball.

Aaron Jones Sr. added a touchdown on the day, while Wentz and Jefferson connected for a two-point conversion. A fumble recovery returned to Green Bay's 1-yard line turned into a Jordan Mason score, and an interception led to another Jefferson touchdown to seal the deal.

Green Bay will hit the road to face the New York Jets next Sunday while Minnesota will head to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears, both scheduled to kickoff at 1:00 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 5 best NFL Sunday afternoon games from Week 1
articles.summary: NFL Sunday delivered an exciting slate of Week 1 matchups, including several games that came down to the final moments. Here are the five best games from the...
articles.body:
The NFL Sunday season opener put together some great matchups, and they didn't disappoint. There were numerous battles that went down to the wire and gave fans a thrilling Sunday afternoon.

There were games that went into overtime, came down to the final plays, and even produced video-game-like final scores. Week 1 delivered for fans who were eager to have football back on Sundays.

Here were the five best games from NFL Sunday's first Week 1 afternoon slate:

Aug 22, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up before the game between the Cleveland Browns and the Bills at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Texans came into the game with an odd trend of really having quarterback Josh Allen's number. Oftentimes, these are relatively low-scoring games. Not this time.

Allen and C.J. Stroud went toe-to-toe in a shootout that came down to the wire. Houston had a chance late in the game but couldn't come through.

The Bills pulled away with a 36-31 victory, and both teams got off to hot starts offensively.

Aug 22, 2026; Detroit , Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) on the sidelines before their preseason game against the Washington Commanders at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

New Orleans and Detroit put on a show in Motown. After the Lions took a 21-0 lead halfway through the third quarter, Tyler Shough and the Saints made a furious comeback.

Both teams traded fourth-quarter blows and eventually went to overtime. That's when things got even more thrilling. The Lions took a 31-24 overtime lead.

Shough and the Saints drove down the field and responded with a touchdown. With less than two minutes left in overtime, the Saints went for the win but came up short on the two-point conversion. This was the NFL's best game of the afternoon.

Aug 21, 2026; Pittsburgh , Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy talks with quarterback Aaron Rodgers during warms up for a game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Steelers' 20-13 victory wasn't pretty, but it was a close game the whole way through. Bijan Robinson put the Falcons on his back and single-handedly kept them in the game. On the other side of it all, T.J. Watt delivered in a big way.

Watt recorded a critical pick-six that proved to be the difference in a defensive grinder of a matchup. The Falcons don't have any pushovers on the defensive side of the ball. Their secondary is legit and gave Pittsburgh fits.

The Steelers started the Mike McCarthy era with a win and a typical Steelers-type victory.

Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles

Aug 15, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) warms up before a game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Eagles and Commanders didn't need a fifth period of play, but they did have a game that went down to the wire in Philadelphia.

The Eagles couldn't quite put the Commanders away despite making big plays on offense throughout the day. Jayden Daniels had a chance to send his team to overtime late in the game.

However, a questionable play call by Washington came up short, and Philly got the win.

Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) warms up before the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

This matchup is what happens when two middle schoolers play a round of Madden and put the settings on rookie. In all seriousness, it was a shootout from start to finish. Caleb Williams and Bryce Young squared off in a battle of former No. 1 overall picks.

The biggest producers, though, were the Bears' running backs. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 224 rushing yards and four rushing scores. Even though the Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory, it was a pretty exciting game for fans to watch.

That is, of course, unless you prefer defensive battles. Then it was brutal to watch.

articles.title: Ravens overcome injuries, penalties in dominant Week 1 win over Colts
articles.summary: Jesse Minter led the Ravens to a complete victory over the Colts in his head coaching debut.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens throttled the Indianapolis Colts in a 41-23 victory on Sunday afternoon to get their 2026 season and the Jesse Minter era off to a 1-0 start.

"It's surreal a little bit, honestly." Minter said after his head coaching debut. "I don't know if it's actually hit me yet. But it's a blessing to be where I'm at – again, such appreciation for the opportunity given to me by this organization."

Led by first-time play-caller Declan Doyle and two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson , Baltimore's offense racked up 502 yards (7.9 yards per play) despite several penalties by the offensive line. Jackson was brilliant through the air, completing 17 of his 25 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown and throwing in 40 yards and another score on the ground for good measure. He looked right at home in Doyle's new-look, under-center heavy offense, and when the system broke down, his signature elusiveness took over. On one miraculous play, he somehow ducked under two oncoming pass rushers and scrambled 16 yards for a first down.

When asked about his latest magic trick, Jackson said that he was "just playing football." He also shouted out Doyle for "dialing it up" on offense and praised the team for finishing the game strong.

Wide receiver Zay Flowers flew around the field for 150 receiving yards on just five catches before leaving the game late in the first half with hamstring injury. Running back Derrick Henry averaged 6.0 yards per carry and scored three times on the ground to pass Marcus Allen for third place on the NFL's all-time rushing touchdown list.

The Colts offense surprised Minter's defense with seven straight passes to start the game, putting the secondary on its back foot and setting up a Jonathan Taylor touchdown. The opening possession stirred painful memories of the Zach Orr defenses that folded all too easily in the past two seasons.

"Defensively, I thought I didn't do a great job on the first drive," Minter explained. "They had us on our heels a little bit, and then I felt like we really settled in on defense and did some good things and attacked the football well."

Baltimore responded by forced three punts and two turnovers on Indianapolis' next five drives. Notably, those turnovers were forced by Smith and cornerback Marlon Humphrey , two veteran defenders who, by their own admission, played below their standard last year.

"I feel like the start of the game kind of went against their identity, in my opinion," linebacker Roquan Smith said. "Those guys [are] normally known for running the ball…There are highs and lows, but we took a deep breath, came to the sideline, and [said] 'Hey, this isn't us.'"

Edge rusher Trey Hendrickson did not notch any sacks in his Ravens debut, but he consistently moved Colts quarterback Daniel Jones off his spot with eight pressures on just 26 pass rushes, per Next Gen Stats . The 31-year-old appears to be worth every penny of the massive $112 million free agent deal he signed in Baltimore this offseason.

And just because John Harbaugh is no longer in Baltimore does not mean special teams are not an emphasis. In Anthony Levine 's debut as a coordinator, the Ravens consistently won the field position battle. Rookie punter Ryan Eckley landed all three of his punts inside the Colts' 20-yard line, and returners Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester both ripped off long returns.

Second-year kicker Tyler Loop entered Week 1 under the microscope after an up-and-down preseason and the signing of former 49ers kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad. He made both of his field goal attempts and all five of his extra points. His 57-yard field goal was a career-long, while his 45-yarder effectively clinched the Ravens' victory in the fourth quarter.

"My confidence in him has never really shaken," Minter said of his young kicker. "Obviously, you have to make kicks and things like that, and in the preseason, he had a couple of mishaps. But just the work ethic and the trust in the process in so many different things that he's been working on, I expected nothing less. I am really happy for him that he performed that way today."

All told, the Ravens controlled the game from start to finish and more than doubled the Colts' in yardage (506 to 251). 10 penalties for 86 yards and injuries to Flowers (hamstring) and rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) were the only blemishes on a deeply satisfying victory for the team. Minter did not have updates on either wideout following the game.

The Ravens will return to Baltimore brimming with confidence after beating a talented, well-coached Colts squad. They will take on the New Orleans Saints in their home opener next week, likely as heavy favorites. However, the Saints barely lost to the Detroit Lions in overtime on Sunday afternoon; this could be the kind of early-season trap game the Ravens have fallen into multiple times in recent years.

articles.title: Week 2 NFL Power Rankings: 49ers, Seahawks Bengals, Bills Rise as Packers, Patriots Implode
articles.summary: The wait is over, with Sunday kicking off the main slate of Week 1 action to really begin the start […]
articles.body:
The wait is over, with Sunday kicking off the main slate of Week 1 action to really begin the start of the 2026 NFL season. It's never wise to overreact too much to a single game, especially this early, but we can make some assessments of all 32 teams right now.

Let's dive into our Week 2 NFL power rankings, evaluating how teams performed in their regular-season opener. We'll also have updates after Sunday Night Football ( Dallas Cowboys vs New York Giants ) and Monday Night Football ( Denver Broncos vs Kansas City Chiefs ).

The Seattle Seahawks demonstrated why they are the best team in the NFL right now in their Week 1 win over New England . Even with backup quarterback Drew Lock forced into action, reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered the game-changing play the offense needed and Seattle's defense put the team on its back for much of the night. Even if Darnold were to miss the next two weeks, the building blocks of the Seahawks roster can beat the Cardinals (Week 2) and Commanders (Week 3).

Josh Allen finally exorcised one of his biggest demons in Week 1, beating the Houston Texans with an outstanding performance against an elite defense that has shut him down in the past. Adding DJ Moore (100 yards, 1 touchdown on 5 receptions) clearly is an elevator for Buffalo's passing game and it appears Buffalo might also be getting that breakthrough year from tight end Dalton Kincaid . If the Bills can do this against Houston's defense, the Lions are in serious trouble on that side of the ball in Week 2.

What a difference-maker it is for the Baltimore Ravens to have a healthy Lamar Jackson behind a quality offensive line. Naturally, this team looks even better when the Ravens' defense plays up to its talent level, and that should happen more consistently in 2026 under head coach Jesse Minter, with pass rusher Trey Hendrickson now leading that front seven. On Sunday, Baltimore showcased why it might be the best team in the AFC.

If the San Francisco 49ers are going to have a defense capable of playing at the level we saw in Australia, this is one of the five best NFL teams in 2026. Even with rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling out for a month-plus , there are more than enough offensive weapons on San Francisco 's offense for Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy , and Christian McCaffrey to put up 27-plus points a game. An outstanding offense, great coaching, and an above-average defense can take San Francisco to the Super Bowl.

Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos have a great opportunity on Monday Night Football. The Chiefs' weaknesses right now align perfectly with Denver's strengths, and that creates a great chance for Nix to demonstrate that these two AFC West rivals are simply on different tiers right now. We're particularly intrigued to see what offensive coordinator Davis Webb can draw up in his first game as play-caller.

Kamari Lassiter will lose a lot of sleep for the next few nights over dropping that game-sealing interception and then surrendering the game-deciding touchdown. Starting 0-1 is a blow for the Houston Texans, but DeMeco Ryans at least has to feel good about C.J. Stroud's performance (106.7 passer rating, 7.2 YPA and 2-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio) and what Houston got from David Montgomery and Woody Marks (102 yards, two touchdowns on 29 carries). Dropping this one hurts, and it makes it imperative that the defense turns things around in Week 2 against Joe Burrow and the Bengals .

So, clearly the Los Angeles Rams ' strategy for travel blew up in their face. What is far more troubling is that for as talented as this offense is, its third-down issues remain. A season after ranking 17th in third-down conversion rate (39.6 percent), Los Angeles went 2-for-9 on Thursday night. To make matters worse, All-Pro edge rusher Myles Garrett is now on injured reserve after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery. Is it time to panic in Los Angeles? No, but the "Dream Team" label is clearly a curse.

Ben Johnson stated before the season that he wanted the Chicago Bears offense to set single-season NFL records in 2026. If Week 1 is any indication of what's to come, that might be on the table. Caleb Williams had some MVP-caliber moments and Chicago's rushing attack seemed to already be in midseason form. So, what prevents a team that dropped 45 points in three quarters from being even higher in the NFL power rankings? Chicago's defense might be even worse than feared.

Not exactly an inspiring performance by the Philadelphia Eagles. Washington came within a two-point conversion of sending this one into overtime at Lincoln Financial Field. Turnovers and third-down woes (6-for-14) weren't necessarily the problem for the Eagles offense, but making it into the red zone on just three of 12 drives isn't exactly a ringing endorsement of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion against this Commanders defense. We came away from Sunday believing the gap between Philadelphia and Dallas is closer than some may realize.

If the Cincinnati Bengals have a viable defense, another Super Bowl contender has emerged in a wide-open AFC. Takeaways aren't the best way to measure a defense, as they can be sporadic, but Cincinnati also fared pretty well in Week 1 on simply containing the Buccaneers ' offense. The fan base and organization should be feeling great right now because this absolutely looks like the best team around Joe Burrow since the Bengals made consecutive trips to the AFC Championship Game from 2021-22.

We remain high on the Dallas Cowboys heading into their Sunday Night Football matchup. This remains one of the league's best offenses, with the lone thing separating Dallas from becoming a top-tier NFC team in 2026 being its defense. Similar to the 49ers, all the Cowboys really need is for defensive coordinator Christian Parker to get this unit to a top-15 level. There is a chance of that happening, and even if this is just a top-20 defense, Dallas is a wild-card contender who can challenge Philadelphia for the NFC East crown.

Week 1's matchup against Cleveland essentially felt like a tune-up game for the Jacksonville Jaguars . Trevor Lawrence got to show his mastery of Liam Coen's offense and that his production late in 2025 ( 13-1 TD-INT ratio and 113.5 passer rating in final five games) was no fluke. Meanwhile, Jacksonville's defense feasted on the Browns' offense like it should. This team might be lower in our NFL power rankings entering Week 2 than Jacksonville fans want to see, but it can absolutely prove it's in the cream of the crop in the AFC if it beats Denver next Sunday.

The Detroit Lions took a 21-0 lead at home over New Orleans in the midway point of the fourth quarter. That's when the wheels fell off, with Detroit's offense putting up 23 total yards on its next two possessions while the defense surrendered four consecutive scoring drives covering 274 yards, with 24 points put on the board. The Lions' offense managed to take it to overtime and find the end zone on its first extra possession, but the defense gave it right back, and Detroit got the 31-30 win instead of a tie entirely because New Orleans opted to roll the dice on a two-point conversion.

There are a few reasons to be concerned with the New England Patriots coming out of Week 1. First, All-Pro wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss 4-6 weeks with a high-ankle sprain and this Patriots offense likely won't see him at 100 percent for two-plus months. Romeo Doubs clearly isn't suited for that No. 1 role either. That only puts a bigger microscope on Drake Maye , who has a 7-7 TD-INT ratio with 24 sacks taken in his last five games. The issues might not prove costly in Week 2 at home against Pittsburgh , but they could be responsible for losses in a two-week stretcha fter that against the Jaguars and Bills on the road.

The final score (39-22) wasn't a true indication of how close this NFC North game was. However, the Minnesota Vikings proved they are far better at handling adversity and stepping up in critical moments. Minnesota didn't wave the white flag when Kyler Murray got knocked out on an unnecessary hit in the first quarter, nor did this team wave the white flag when it trailed by two scores late in the third quarter. Murray will return, and the coaching staff and locker room now have a 1-0 record with momentum to carry over into the rest of the season.

The Green Bay Packers imploded on Sunday afternoon in Minnesota. It truly started with Matt LaFleur's dumbfounding decision to turn down 3 points for an eight-point lead in the fourth quarter to go for it on 4th-and-1, an attempt that failed. Did Minnesota get bailed out by highly questionable penalties on its go-ahead touchdown drive? Sure. However, that doesn't cast away LaFleur's bad decision, nor does it overshadow how this team just imploded after giving up that touchdown. There's a ton of talent on this Packers roster, but the inability to maintain composure and close games in the fourth quarter is an awful sign for an organization with playoff aspirations.

We are lower on the Kansas City Chiefs than the consensus NFL power rankings, and a few of the reasons why should be demonstrated on Monday night. Kansas City's standout left tackle Josh Simmons remains sidelined by an injury, and there are added concerns about this new-look secondary with Chamarri Conner sidelined. In Patrick Mahomes ' first game back from ACL surgery and with the inexperience on Kansas City's defense, this feels like a matchup that highlights this team still isn't ready to return to peak form.

Not what anyone expected from this Los Angeles Chargers offense in the first game of the Mike McDaniel era. Days ahead of this Week 1 matchup, Jim Harbaugh shared his belief that Justin Herbert would go down as the best quarterback in NFL history. That young passer just took 3 sacks, threw an interception, and finished with an 83.7 passer rating in a 12-point loss at home to the Cardinals. Given Harbaugh's recent track record, see his comments on J.J. McCarthy , perhaps we should worry more about his talent evaluations.

If it could go wrong for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first half of Sunday's game, it did. Right when it seemed like some semblance of momentum was being regained, Baker Mayfield was stripped of the football at the 4-yard line, and Cincinnati recovered it in the end zone and then answered with an 80-yard touchdown drive. Three-turnover games are obviously an outlier, but this team-wide performance did nothing to erase criticism of the Buccaneers for retaining head coach Todd Bowles.

The Carolina Panthers might not have come out of Week 1 with the win, but there are reasons for optimism. Jalen Coker is clearly ready to take that next big leap this season, and quarterback Bryce Young took advantage of Chicago's secondary. Plus, the rest of the NFC South didn't look all that impressive on Sunday. Someone has to win this division, and the Panthers' season debut provided a few pieces of evidence to believe they can.

Things looked bleak for the New Orleans Saints in the third quarter, trailing 21-0 with no real semblance of hope. Tyler Shough had turned it over three times, and some in the Bayou might've started thinking about the 2027 quarterback class. Then, the Saints offense came marching back to send it to overtime. The gamble for the game-winning two-point try backfired, but New Orleans demonstrated in Week 1 that it has the fortitude and talent to compete for the division.

Beating a team led by a third-string quarterback because of a pick-six is not a ringing endorsement of the Pittsburgh Steelers . Aaron Rodgers (5.5 yards per attempt, 3.4 QB rating on 40 attempts) looked like a 42-year-old starting quarterback, and the Steelers couldn't run the football effectively (2.8 yards per carry on 21 attempts). Pittsburgh might be 1-0, but that performance did nothing to make us feel like it is a viable playoff contender.

There are plenty of reasons to be intrigued with the New York Giants this season. A healthy trio of Jaxson Dart , Cam Skattebo , and Malik Nabers will generate plenty of explosive plays, and tight end Isaiah Likely could be primed for a breakout year. Defensively, this front seven's ability to generate pressure will rival some of the top units around the league. We just do not have enough faith in New York's secondary nor its offensive core staying on the field and playing consistently well.

The Arizona Cardinals offense was already good enough to win three to four games this season. In Sunday's stunning Week 1 victory over the Chargers, it was Arizona's defense and special-teams units that made the difference. No one is going to mistake this club for a playoff contender, but maybe six or seven wins is on the table for Arizona in 2026.

The Washington Commanders fought back and came within a failed two-point conversion of sending this one into overtime in Philadelphia. While it might have ultimately ended in a loss, quarterback Jayden Daniels played reasonably well given the defense he faced, and rookie Antonio Williams made his first big play in the league. Victories will determine if Dan Quinn keeps his job or not, but we see positives for Washington today.

The Las Vegas Raiders beat a team they were supposed to. That might sound like a knock, but it's something this team couldn't do last season, especially when a quarterback threw two interceptions. Ashton Jeanty (147 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns) largely carried this offense on Sunday, and Maxx Crosby showed why he can still be a game-wrecker. There's just no room for Las Vegas to move up on a Sunday where other teams looked better in terms of the eye test.

Sunday's loss in the home opener against Baltimore should serve as a reminder of just how many tiers below the best NFL teams the Indianapolis Colts are. Daniel Jones is coming off an Achilles injury, and it's not like the Colts' offensive line is as good as it used to be. The ceiling for this offense just isn't what we saw during its peak moments in 2025, and if the Colts' secondary struggles like it did Sunday in the months to come, a sub-.500 record is possible.

Dare we say that the New York Jets could be a competitive and entertaining team in 2026? The Jets' offensive line looked as good as we could ask for, allowing Geno Smith to operate from a clean pocket with an array of on-target throws, all the while this run game consistently gained chunks of yards. New York might still be headed for a three-game losing streak (Packers, Lions, and Bears in Weeks 2 to 4), but we also believe it won't be in the mix for a top-three pick in 2027.

That was actually a closer game than we expected for the Atlanta Falcons considering they had to roll with a third-string quarterback with little time to prepare. With that said, Sunday also serves as a reminder of how bad Atlanta's quarterback situation truly is because the injured alternatives ( Michael Penix Jr . and Tua Tagovailoa ) are still bottom-tier starters. It's going to be a rough season for Atlanta, but at least Bijan Robinson will get his numbers.

The rebuilding Miami Dolphins are a bad football team. Not entirely shocking. Malik Willis doesn't really have the supporting cast to be successful, and opponents can throw everything they have to stop De'Von Achane while putting up points against a bottom-10 defense. This is going to be a weekly theme for Miami, and they are firmly in the mix for the No. 1 overall pick.

Our expectations for the Tennessee Titans in 2025 were admittedly low, but we didn't think it would look this bad in Week 1. Brian Daboll's debut as the Titans' play-caller went about as poorly as one could imagine, with Cam Ward finishing under 50 net passing yards on more than 20 dropbacks before garbage time hit. Equally troubling is this defense under Robert Saleh, which made Geno Smith look like the standout quarterback we saw a few seasons ago in Seattle. It might only be one game, but Tennessee easily looks like it will be one of the worst NFL teams this season.

Week 1 left no doubt that the Cleveland Browns are the worst NFL team in 2026. Deshaun Watson is abysmal as a starter, and it feels like a distinct possibility that Browns head coach Todd Monken makes a change to Shedeur Sanders by the home opener in Week 3. Expectedly, this defense also appears poised to take a step back with Jim Schwartz and Myles Garrett gone. On the bright side for Cleveland, it's the favorite for the No. 1 pick.

articles.summary: The first week of NFL action brought with it some extraordinary performances, including from players overlooked in fantasy.

The first week of NFL action brought with it some extraordinary performances, including from players overlooked in fantasy.

Who are those players, and why should managers keep their eyes on them amid a pursuit of a league championship?

Find out in this look at the Week 2 waiver wire.

The third-year wide receiver developed chemistry with quarterback Bryce Young last season and into the playoffs. It looks like this season could represent the evolution of their on-field relationship, if the first week of the 2026 season is any indication.

Coker caught eight-of-nine passes for 138 yards and two touchdowns in a 59-37 loss to the Bears.

That should be enough to earn him a top-five finish among wide receivers in PPR leagues and the attention of fantasy managers.

With defenses likely focused on reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan, it will open up opportunities for Coker. More importantly, if the Panthers defense performs the way it did Sunday afternoon, the team will be slinging the ball around the field as it attempts to keep up with opponents.

Advantage, Coker, and managers with him on the roster.

He will not produce numbers like his Week 1 stats all season, but he should be a reliable option in an offense that has proved it can score.

Coker is available in over 71 percent of leagues, per Fantasy Pros .

Plenty of fantasy managers slept on David Montgomery, about 51 percent according to Fantasy Pros , a stat that should change dramatically following an extraordinary performance against Buffalo.

The 29-year-old back rushed 20 times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added three receptions for 19 yards and a receiving touchdown.

He was the heart and soul of the Houston Texans offense and proved that he can help take some of the pressure off of starting quarterback CJ Stroud.

Perhaps, but the offensive playcalling made it abundantly clear that the Texans have big plans for the veteran back this season. As a result, managers should, too.

Get him on your bench, at best, and monitor his usage in the coming weeks to determine if he flashes consistent starting potential.

Gesicki caught five-of-seven passes for 78 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

He was a consistent option for quarterback Joe Burrow and the team's leading receiver, boosting the offense when Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase were held to five total receptions.

A safety blanket for Burrow, especially in the face of the pass rush against a so-so offensive line, Gesicki is a potentially game-changing fantasy pickup on a pass-happy team.

Not at the level of a Trey McBride or Brock Bowers, but Gesicki is potentially in that next tier.

The Bengals pass-catcher is inexplicably rostered in just one percent of leagues, per Fantasy Pros .

articles.title: Bills edge Texans while Bears beat Panthers in NFL record-setting opener
articles.summary: Buffalo's Josh Allen finally managed his first triumph at Houston in a thrilling win over the Texans on Sunday while Chicago bested Carolina in the highest-s...
articles.body:
Buffalo 's Josh Allen finally managed his first triumph at Houston in a thrilling win over the Texans on Sunday while Chicago bested Carolina in the highest-scoring opening weekend game in NFL history.

Allen had been 0-4 in prior games at Houston. But the 2024 NFL Most Valuable Player kicked off his 2026 campaign with a masterclass, passing for 334 yards and two touchdowns, and running for two more touchdowns.

"We do like Reliant Stadium! Woohoo!" joked Allen, after wrapping up the last-gasp 36-31 victory in new coach Joe Brady's debut.

"Feels good to start the season off right. Obviously, Coach Joe getting his first win as an NFL head coach... really happy for him. Called a heck of a game."

Allen gave Buffalo the lead in the dying seconds on a stunning 34-yard pass to Joshua Palmer , who raced through the Texans' vaunted defense for a touchdown.

But it was the Bills' own great defensive stand that secured the win.

Houston drove to the Bills' nine-yard line and appeared set to push in for the winning score until Buffalo's Greg Rousseau sacked Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud , and Terrel Bernard recovered a fumble to ensure victory.

"Our defense shows up big when they need it the most," said Allen.

Chicago's Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more in the Bears' madcap 59-37 victory at Carolina -- the 12th-highest scoring NFL game of all time, and a record for opening weekend.

The Bears' explosive offense managed two touchdowns in each quarter, pulling clear in the second half. D'Andre Swift rushed for three touchdowns, but still insisted his team should have won by more.

"We'll take the win. Fifty-nine points is amazing, it's awesome. But should have been worse," he said.

Detroit edged visiting New Orleans 31-30 in an overtime thriller.

Jared Goff threw a four-yard touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown in overtime but New Orleans answered when Tyler Shough hit Noah Fant on an eight-yard touchdown pass.

The Saints rejected a tying conversion kick attempt and went for a two-point conversion.

But Shough -- who had passed for a monster 410 yards including three touchdowns -- could not find his man, and the Lions were winners.

"We're always going to be aggressive. That's our mindset," said Shough.

"It just sucks... It was just one play away. It's football."

Baltimore 's Lamar Jackson completed 17-of-25 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown and ran for another touchdown, as the Ravens won their first game under new coach Jesse Minter 41-23 at Indianapolis .

Derrick Henry 's three rushing touchdowns propelled the veteran running back to 125 across his career -- rising to third on the all-time NFL list, behind Emmitt Smith's record 164 and LaDainian Tomlinson's 145.

"It's cool... shout-out to everybody that helped me get to this point," said Henry, hailing his quarterback Jackson as "the best player in the league, for a long time."

Mike LaFleur steered Arizona to a surprise 26-14 road win over the Chargers in his first-ever game as head coach.

Leading 16-14 in the fourth quarter, the Cardinals' special teams unit blocked a punt for a turnover just three yards from the Los Angeles end zone, and converted for touchdown.

Minnesota lost new starting quarterback Kyler Murray to concussion from a gruesome tackle early against NFC North rivals Green Bay .

But the Vikings scored 29 unanswered points in a late rampage to win 39-22.

Philadelphia survived a late Washington rally to win 24-22, after the Commanders' game-tying two point conversion attempt failed.

In Sunday's other games, Aaron Rodgers ' Pittsburgh beat Atlanta 20-13, while Trevor Lawrence threw for four touchdowns as Jacksonville crushed Cleveland 34-10.

Joe Burrow steered Cincinnati to a 33-27 victory over Tampa Bay, the New York Jets beat Tennessee 23-10, and Las Vegas beat Miami 27-13.

And the Los Angeles Rams were hit by news that star defensive end Myles Garrett will undergo knee surgery following their loss to San Francisco in Australia.

articles.title: Eagles hold off Commanders with late stop, but don't blame Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: You can't blame Jayden Daniels for the Washington Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1.
articles.body:
You can't blame Jayden Daniels for the Washington Commanders ' 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1.

Washington played good enough defense — at least for the first 52 minutes of the game — to win. That was the good news. Daniels also heated up late, hitting rookie Antonio Williams for a touchdown with 1:01 remaining to give the Commanders a chance to tie the game.

But the 2-point try — a shovel pass to backup tight end Jake Bates — was no good. The Eagles recovered the onsides kick and ran out the clock for an ugly, workmanlike victory.

The Commanders' offense struggled to find rhythm all game. In his first NFL game calling plays, Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough had the misfortune of going up against savvy Vic Fangio, one of the great defensive minds of his generation. The results mostly favored Fangio and the Eagles.

Washington also missed on an earlier chance to tie after Daniels' TD pass to Stefon Diggs cut Philly's lead to 17-15. After scoring, Diggs bear-hugged the goalpost, which earned his team a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty , which was enforced on the extra-point try.

That turned a potential game-tying 2-point try into a 48-yard extra-point try. The kick was good, but the Commanders never were able to level the score.

Blough's new offense didn't start looking right until the fourth quarter, when Daniels and the Commanders were forced to go tempo to try to fight back. They came up just a little short.

After opening the game with a field goal, the Commanders went into a rut offensively. On their next four series, they gained only one first down and 13 total yards.

Using a lot of heavy sets (two and three tight ends often) early, Washington didn't run the ball well enough for formations that should help the run game. On top of that, there were no real vertical threats.

The Eagles stuck with a lot of two-deep coverages, knowing their front could harass the Commanders' weakened offensive line and really stress Daniels when it came to making big pass plays or breaking off game-changing scrambles. The strategy worked for most of the game.

Blough spoke this preseason about wanting to limit the hits and sacks on Daniels this season. That element was nominally a success Sunday, as Washington allowed only two QB hits and one sack. Yet the passing game was out of sync and the entire process sped up because of the Eagles' pressure.

One of the biggest changes Blough has introduced was on display in the opener: the lack of zone reads that made Daniels so dangerous the past few seasons. Daniels tried to rally the Commanders as a scrambler, and he ripped off a 16-yard beauty in the fourth quarter. Those chances were too few and far between.

Daniels found Williams — who was active ahead of vets Luke McCaffrey and Treylon Burks — for a 33-yard catch on third-and-14 with the Commanders trailing, 17-9, early in the fourth quarter. Williams also had a 16-yard catch down to the Eagles' 1-yard line in the first half, setting up their touchdown before halftime, and he scored late to give the Commanders a chance. It would be a shock if he wasn't a consistent part of the offense after being their best weapon in Week 1.

Terry McLaurin didn't grab his first reception, one of two on the game, until the 4:30 mark of the fourth quarter. Diggs finished with four catches for 55 yards and the score, but they came on nine targets. Diggs' brain-fart penalty late didn't help matters, even if the TD throw and catch were clean.

The Commanders couldn't run the ball all that effectively. The offensive line was under fire most of the game. Daniels had few options to throw to beyond about 5 yards until midway through the fourth quarter. All six Washington penalties were on offense, often putting them in long-yardage situations.

Sure, you can point to the blocked extra-point try on the first touchdown and the late defensive breakdowns as reasons why the Commanders couldn't pull it out. The offense surely left plenty of plays on the field, too.

But blaming Daniels for this one isn't fair. He showed some real spark late after settling in and letting his instincts take over. At the end of the day, that's what Blough wants: his best player making plays with his gut.

Yet there also seemed to be some schematic and operational issues on offense that might need a hard look this week. Early in the game, the play-calling felt very safe — way too passive. Daniels appeared to be at his best in the shotgun running quick tempo late with a gotta-have-it mentality. Some of Blough's desired system changes run anathema to that.

It's Week 1, where fluky things happen. There's little bandwidth for season-long proclamations at this stage. The good news is that Daniels showed that when he gets a chance to create, he can still do it — and there was no clear evidence of the knee, elbow and hamstring injuries that plagued him a year ago.

The bad news is that the Commanders are still finding themselves as an offensive unit. That might take some time to iron out.

articles.title: Packers fall apart after late gamble backfires as Vikings rally to stun rivals without Kyler Murray
articles.summary: The Packers were in control late in the third quarter. But a late gamble backfired, and the Vikings piled on late to stun their NFC North rivals.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers held a 12-point second-half lead Sunday against a Minnesota Vikings team playing without its starting quarterback.

But a late gamble backfired, and a series of questionable calls in Minnesota's favor allowed the Vikings to rally for a stunning 39-22 win. By the end of the game, Minnesota's defense had taken over, and the Vikings piled on with 22 fourth-quarter points.

They secured the win despite playing most of the game without injured starting quarterback Kyler Murray, who left in the first quarter with a concussion following a reckless hit to his head by Packers safety Javon Bullard .

With backup Carson Wentz in at quarterback for the Vikings, Green Bay largely bottled up Minnesota in the first half with the exception of a 39-yard touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson .

The Packers held a 22-10 lead late in third quarter, then faced a pivotal decision early in the fourth.

Green Bay kicked a field goal to extend its lead to 25-17 with 13:21 remaining in regulation. But a Vikings penalty on the kick presented head coach Matt LaFleur with a decision: keep the field goal or take the points off the board for a shot to keep the drive alive.

LaFleur took the points off the board, and the Packers went for it on fourth and a long 1. They didn't get it. Vikings defenders stuffed Jordan Love 's sneak, and the Vikings took over on downs.

The Packers then appeared to stop the the ensuing Vikings drive short of midfield. But a questionable roughing the passer penalty on a third-down hit of Wentz extended the drive.

Vikings capitalize after getting bailed out again

Green Bay's defense then appeared to come up with another play, this time in the end zone with an interception of Wentz. But another borderline penalty — this time holding on Xavier McKinney — bailed Wentz out and gave the Vikings life once again.

The Vikings capitalized on their good fortune. Aaron Jones ran for a touchdown on the next play, and a 2-point conversion gave Minnesota a 25-22 lead.

Then the Vikings piled on. On the ensuing Green Bay possession, the Vikings forced a fumble on a third-down sack of Jordan Love.

They recovered the ball in the red zone, and converted the turnover into a Jordan Mason touchdown for a 32-22 lead.

Two Packers plays later, James Pierre intercepted Love, and the Vikings converted that turnover into Jefferson's second touchdown catch of the day and a 39-22 lead. What not long before was a game that Green Bay controlled had turned into a Vikings blowout and "Skol" chants throughout U.S. Bank Stadium.

Big early win in one of NFL's toughest divisions

The rally for the Vikings acts a a tone-setter in what projects to be a very competitive NFC North and a reprieve after they lost Murray early. It's unclear when Murray will play again, but the Vikings got enough big plays out of Wentz on Sunday to pull out the win.

Wentz finished the day completing 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards with 3 touchdowns and 0 turnovers. Jefferson did the bulk of the damage on the receiving end as he tallied 8 catches for 92 yards, 2 touchdowns and the 2-point conversion.

Justin Jefferson , Vikings defense step up

Jefferson's touchdown tally matched his total from his entire season in 2025, a down year in which he didn't catch a touchdown at home. His effort Sunday signaled his return to All-Pro form, even while playing with a backup quarterback.

And an aggressive defense helmed by coordinator Brian Flores got the job done late against a dangerous Packers offense. The Vikings sacked Love four times and forced two late turnovers to seal the win.

Love was productive until his late mistakes, completing 21 of 42 passes for 387 yards with 2 touchdowns. But his fourth-quarter interception and fumble accounted for both of Green Bays's turnovers and allowed Minnesota to seal the win.

The late breakdown spoiled a breakout effort from Christian Watson , who tallied 6 catches for 147 yards and 2 touchdowns in his first career game as Green Bay's clear No. 1 receiving option, coming off an offseason in which he signed a four-year, $92 million contract extension.

The Packers will seek to exact their revenge on Nov. 11 when they host the Vikings in matchup that could carry playoff implications.

articles.title: Giants Beat Cowboys, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Dak, Dart, Odell, Skattebo, Lamb, Top Players
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart and the New York Giants limited Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys to just two second-half possessions to secure a 28-20 Week 1 home victory on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart and the New York Giants limited Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys to just two second-half possessions to secure a 28-20 Week 1 home victory on Sunday night.

The Cowboys were a narrow 3-point favorite ahead of their matchup against the Giants, per Fanduel Sportsbook , but New York sports stayed hot on Sunday with the season opening Giants win.

Tempers were flaring early in the Week 1 NFC East battle, with Dallas and New York eager to get a leg up on one another after finishing last season's head-to-head matchup 1-1.

Dallas grabbed a Week 2, 40-37 overtime win, while New York walked away with a 34-17 win in the season finale. Despite this, neither team made the postseason, with Dallas finishing second in the division (7-9) and New York last (4-13).

Giants' legendary wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. made his return to MetLife Stadium on Sunday, suited up in red, white and blue for the first time since 2018.

He did not see the field, but former Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton believes he still has what it takes to be the elite receiver he once was.

"... He has that type of shock and awe, I guess a wow factor, so to speak. But I think he brings a lot of experience," Slayton said, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . "He still has juice, too. I think he's shown that. He can still play for sure."

The 33-year-old was drafted by the Giants in 2014 with the No. 12 overall pick.

A quick three-and-out for Dallas led to New York notching the first touchdown of the game, eating up the clock with a 6:13 drive that finished with Skattebo finding the end zone on a 3-yard run.

Dallas' first score came in the second after Prescott marched the Cowboys down the field on an 85-yard drive, finishing the possession with a short connection to CeeDee Lamb.

It was tit-for-tat after that, as New York's Tyrone Tracy Jr. fumbled it away, then Prescott threw an interception on the following possession.

The Giants found the final score of the half behind a 15-yard connection between Dart and Isaiah Likely to take a 14-7 lead.

To open the third, New York ran the clock down to just under seven minutes before Dart connected with Likely once more for a score. Prescott and the Cowboys responded with a Javonte Williams rushing touchdown.

Again, the Giants milked the clock in the fourth with an 8:11 possession, resulting in a Devin Singletary receiving touchdown to put New York up 28-14.

Another quick response from Prescott to Williams for a touchdown brought Dallas within one score, but the Giants were able to convert on third downs and run down the clock to secure the win.

New York will head west to face the Los Angeles Rams next week for a Monday night showdown, with kickoff scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Dallas will host the Washington Commanders next Sunday, scheduled to start at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: John Harbaugh's Giants on full display in bruising win over Cowboys to kick off NFL season
articles.summary: Methodic runs, more mature Jaxson Dart, and chewing clock led to a perfect start to the John Harbaugh era for the New York Giants against the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body: For months, the talk throughout the tri-state area had been about this new era for the New York Giants. How could it not be, as John Harbaugh, after almost two decades with the Baltimore Ravens, signed on as the next Giants head coach. It was a post he said he felt pride assuming, understanding the expectations and pedigree he was supposed to bring back to a prestigious franchise that had been reeling until his arrival. Well, the Harbaugh era kicked off in the best way possible for Giants fans on Sunday night, as they took down the Dallas Cowboys, 28-20, in the hard-nosed fashion that was to be expected with this new regime. From the very beginning, the Giants’ defense forced a three-and-out and got a sold-out MetLife Stadium crowd on their feet as Jaxson Dart and company took the field for the first time in 2026. What ensued was a 10-play, 83-yard drive that took 6:13 off the first-quarter clock and resulted in a Cam Skattebo touchdown. While Harbaugh may not have enjoyed Skattebo’s celebratory backflip, the 7-0 lead on the opening drive was exactly what this coaching staff wanted to see with its top offensive weapons out there for the first time this season. Long drives were a theme for the Giants in this game, as they used a bruising run game, and some creative play-calls that came at the right time, to fluster the Cowboys’ defense, which was supposed to be an improved unit this season.
